concepts.title: RANGE
concepts.logline: At dawn on what looks like an alien volcanic world, steep peaks with summits in every pure colour rise above a sea of cloud. Then the tallest crimson mountain tears itself out of the ground and climbs into the sky. It turns out to be a giant lacquered hexagonal tower, and the whole range turns out to be a drum of 288 sharpened colour pencils. The range dances to the music. In the last shot, the crimson pencil comes down and draws the same skyline we started on, so it is mountains all the way down.
concepts.surprise: 1) 10.8 s to 14.0 s (main reveal). The crimson summit, which we have read as a mountain for 10 seconds, rumbles and rises straight up out of the cloud sea. Under it is a glossy crimson hexagonal tower, and silver-foil lettering ('RANGE  No.01 CADMIUM CRIMSON  ARTIST PIGMENT') slides past the lens like a skyscraper sign. Its white-ringed dipped end clears at 14.0 s and leaves a black hexagonal hole. The viewer suddenly re-reads every previous frame: the wood growth rings were the rock strata, the pigment cores were the coloured summits, the crumbs were the boulders, and the cloud sea was hiding the painted pencil bodies. 2) 16 s to 19 s (second layer). In one continuous pull-back, the 'sky' turns out to be a curved coloured paper backdrop and the low 'sun' turns out to be a round LED studio panel on a stand. The world was a product shoot. 3) 20.5 s to 25.5 s (the crazy part). The mountain range comes alive and plays the music: rings and spirals of pencils pump up and down on every beat. On the last bar all 287 jump together, hang for one frame and slam back down. 4) 28.6 s (loop). The line the crimson pencil has been scratching across the paper turns out, in a high wide shot, to be exactly the skyline from the first frame. The film ends where it began.
concepts.palette: PENCIL PIGMENTS (24-hue curated set, grouped into geological 'colour zones' across the range): Cadmium Crimson #E3122C (hero), Vermilion #FF3B1F, Tangerine #FF7A00, Saffron #FFB300, Lemon #FFE51A, Lime #9BE11E, Emerald #00B85C, Cerulean #1EA0FF, Cobalt #0050FF, Ultramarine #2B2FD9, Electric Violet #7B2BFF, Orchid #C03BFF, Hot Magenta #FF1A8C, Flamingo #FF5FA2, Coral #FF5A4E, Midnight Plum #3A0F5C, Ink #111116, Chalk #F7F7F2 (no teal, and no gold metal anywhere). MATERIALS: Cedar Blond wood #D8A469 with Ring Sienna growth rings #9A5527, a Primer White seam #F2EEE6 at the scalloped paint edge, Silver Foil stamping #C9CDD6, a Satin Midnight Navy anodized drum #161A3A, Warm Snow paper #F5F0E6, a Bone desk #E9E2D6. SKY/SWEEP GRADIENT: Apricot Haze #FFB27A at the horizon, then Rose Dusk #FF6F91, then Orchid Night #7B3FD0, then Deep Violet #2A1458 at the top. LIGHTING: Shots 1 to 3 are an 'alien dawn': one hard, low sun-lamp key (3000K, #FFB070, about 4 degrees elevation, 0.5 degree angular size) gives long violet shadows across the range, with a lilac rim #B49CFF and coral bounce, so the scheme is warm against violet complementaries. Shot 4 opens out into studio light: the LED disc plus two large soft area lights. Shots 5 and 6 are a punchy high-key product look with strong rim streaks on the lacquer, then a raking light across the paper. Colour management is AgX with the Punchy look, and saturation is pushed in the compositor.

shots.description: ALIEN DAWN (frames 1-120). Steep conical peaks rise from a slow luminous cloud sea under an apricot-to-violet sky, with a huge low sun glowing on the horizon. Every summit crown is a different blazing pigment (crimson, cobalt, emerald, magenta, saffron). The slopes are cedar-blond, ringed with dark concentric strata like contour lines, and long violet shadows fall between the peaks. It reads as an alien volcanic range. Fine dust drifts like high-altitude haze.
shots.camera: 28mm, positioned between the cloud-sea level and the summits. Slow dolly forward (about 6 cm of scene travel over 120 frames, at 1 unit = 1 cm) with a gentle rise and 1.5 degrees of roll drift. DOF is OFF (deep focus is essential for the big-scale illusion), aerial depth comes from a compositor mist pass, the sun disc gets a glare/bloom flare, and motion blur is on.
shots.key_elements: About 288 instanced pencils with only the sharpened cones showing above a thin volume slab, the hero crimson pencil as a separate object, an emissive 'sun' disc, a curved gradient sweep acting as the sky, 15k dust motes, crumb 'boulders' on the slopes

shots.description: STRATA (frames 121-228). A low skim across a cobalt-capped slope. The wood growth rings read as eroded sedimentary bands, the sharpener-blade facet ridges as terraces, and the graphite/pigment crumbs and tiny wood-shaving curls as boulders and debris. At the cloud line, the scalloped lacquered cliff edge with its thin white primer seam glints for an instant. The camera crests a saddle and reveals the tallest summit in the range, blazing cadmium crimson in full sun.
shots.camera: 20mm lateral tracking shot, right to left, in a slightly descending arc, with foreground crumbs passing close for strong parallax. It ends by rising over the saddle into a reveal of the crimson peak. DOF off, motion blur on, with a subtle handheld-helicopter noise on rotation.
shots.key_elements: High-LOD pencil cones, micro-displaced wood fibre and facet ridges, crystalline pigment sparkle, GN-scattered crumbs and shaving curls, the volume cloud slab, the low sun

shots.description: UPROOT (frames 229-360). A heroic low angle at the base of the crimson peak. At 10.2 s a tremor runs through it: crumbs skitter down the slopes and the cloud sea ripples. At 10.8 s the entire mountain starts rising, slowly and then accelerating. It tears up through the cloud and exposes a colossal glossy crimson hexagonal tower with foil-stamped lettering that slides past the lens like a skyscraper sign. The dipped, white-ringed end clears at 14.0 s and leaves a dark hexagonal void. The camera tilts up to follow the tower into the sky, then hard-cuts on a sub boom.
shots.camera: 16mm, tripod-like, with a decaying Noise F-modifier shake for the tremor. It then follows the rising tower with an eased tilt-up of about 70 degrees, with slight lag for weight. Deep focus, motion blur on (it smears the lettering as it accelerates).
shots.key_elements: Hero pencil mesh with embossed silver-foil text and a dipped end cap, about 150 baked rigid-body (or keyframed) crumbs falling, the cloud slab disturbed by an animated noise offset, neighbouring pencils' lacquered hex faces appearing as walls of the void

shots.description: THE PULL (frames 361-492). It opens top-down on the black hexagonal well: six coloured lacquer walls dropping into darkness, ringed by a honeycomb of rainbow summits. In one continuous move the camera rockets up and back about 200x in scale while orbiting and tilting to an oblique. The range becomes a tight bundle of 288 colour pencils in a satin navy anodized drum standing on a sheet of paper on a bone desk. The 'sky' is a curved paper sweep and the 'sun' is a round LED studio panel on a yoke and stand. The crimson pencil hovers in the air above, slowly turning.
shots.camera: An exponential altitude curve (constant perceived speed) combined with a 40-degree orbit, ending at a 35-degree oblique. Focal length eases from 24mm to 35mm. DOF ramps from off to f/2.8 at real scale with focus tracking the drum rim, which sells the miniature. The mist pass fades to zero and motion blur is on.
shots.key_elements: Switch from high-LOD to low-LOD pencils, the drum, desk, paper, sweep backdrop, LED panel housing and stand (unseen until now), the hovering hero pencil, the volume slab faded out

shots.description: THE RANGE PLAYS (frames 493-612). The music drops and the mountain range turns into an instrument. Pencils rise and fall in concentric ripples spreading out from the empty centre, with a rotating spiral wave on top, and each downbeat kicks a new ring of pencils up. The colour zones shimmer as tips catch the rim light. On the final bar all 287 pencils jump about 3 cm together, hang for one frame and slam down in a wooden clatter. The crimson pencil above slowly turns tip-down.
shots.camera: 70mm, slow 60-degree orbit around the drum at 25 to 40 degrees elevation, with shallow DOF focused on the front rim. Lacquer highlights streak with motion blur, and there is a subtle push-in on the final leap.
shots.key_elements: A GN height offset driven by wave_amp, wave_phase and beat_pulse inputs keyed from the music's onset/beat times (120 BPM = 12 frames per beat), the hero pencil's rotation, rim lights, studio HDRI reflections on the drum

shots.description: SIGNATURE (frames 613-720). Macro at paper level. The crimson pencil descends tip-first from the top of frame like an inverted crimson mountain falling out of the sky. It touches the fibrous paper at 26.3 s and drags across, its pigment catching only the tops of the paper tooth, drawing a jagged line. At 28.6 s it cuts to a high wide shot: the line is exactly the skyline from shot 1. The pencil lifts out of frame and the word RANGE blind-embosses into the paper under the line on the final music hit. A short hold, then cut to black at 30.0 s.
shots.camera: 100mm macro tracking along the stroke about 1 cm above the paper, with shallow DOF and a focus pull that follows the tip. The final wide is 50mm at 70 degrees looking down, static with a 2% slow push.
shots.key_elements: A dense local paper patch with procedural tooth, a GN stroke mask (Geometry Proximity to a curve times a progress value times a tooth mask), the hero tip constrained to the stroke curve, a skyline curve sampled from the shot-1 silhouette, embossed title text with an animated displacement factor

concepts.build_plan:
UNITS: 1 BU = 1 cm; pencils are real scale (7.5 mm across the flats, 17.5 cm long) and the camera clip-start is 0.005.

1) PENCIL MESH (Python + bmesh, no booleans). Build a parametric grid of 192 angular segments by 260 rings, denser near the tip. Each vertex radius is r(theta, z) = smooth_min(r_hex(theta), r_cone(z)). r_hex is a hexagon with rounded corners (apothem / cos((theta mod 60) - 30), soft-clamped). r_cone is (tip_z - z) * tan(10 degrees). This produces the correct six-arc scalloped paint edge automatically. Store float attributes paint_mask, wood_mask, lead_mask (r below 0.19 cm) and primer_band (distance to the scallop edge). Displace the wood region along the normal with sharpener facet ridges, 0.004 * sin(theta * 14 + z * 3), plus Voronoi chip-outs. Make a slightly rounded or worn tip, with 8 tip variants (sharp, blunt, broken). Build two LODs: about 50k triangles and about 6k triangles. Use the Smooth by Angle modifier.

2) ONE UBER MATERIAL mixed by those attributes. Lacquer: Principled, roughness 0.3, coat 1.0, coat roughness 0.04, orange-peel noise bump. Primer seam: chalk white, roughness 0.6. Wood: object-space radial distance into a Wave texture for growth rings, with noise distortion, plus longitudinal fibre noise stretched 1:40 and a bump. Pigment core: instance colour, roughness 0.55, Voronoi micro-sparkle bump. Per-instance colour comes from an Attribute node (Instancer) reading 'pcol'. Fallback is Object Info Random into a constant-interpolation Color Ramp of the palette.

3) BUNDLE (Geometry Nodes). Lay points on a hex grid (pitch 0.752), keep those inside radius R (about 288 points), and instance the pencil (an LOD switch input). Random Z rotation in 60-degree steps with plus or minus 3 degrees of jitter, and tilt of plus or minus 0.4 degrees. Z offset = A * fBm(xy), giving 3 to 5 major massifs, plus per-pencil jitter, plus a wave term from the inputs wave_amp, wave_phase and beat_pulse. 'pcol' is chosen from palette zones (hue drifts across the field with noise), so the range shows geological colour regions. The hero pencil is removed from the grid and placed as a separate object.

4) HERO PENCIL. Same mesh, crimson. Text objects ('RANGE', 'No.01 CADMIUM CRIMSON', 'ARTIST PIGMENT 7.5') are converted to mesh, inset 0.003 cm into one hex face with a silver-foil material (metallic 1, roughness 0.22). The dipped end cap is crimson with a chalk ring stripe.

5) DEBRIS. Distribute Points on Faces with density times wood_mask, instancing 6 crumb meshes (noise-displaced icospheres) and 3 shaving curls (spiral curves with solidify and a wood material), at 0.005 to 0.04 cm. The shot 3 crumbs on the hero pencil are a baked rigid-body sim of about 150 convex-hull pieces against a static proxy of the neighbouring cones, or keyframed parabolas if the sim misbehaves.

6) ATMOSPHERE. (a) A thin volume slab: Principled Volume with noise-modulated density, sitting at the scallop-line height. It is the 'cloud sea' that hides the hex bodies, and it is only enabled in shots 1 to 3. (b) A compositor Mist pass mixed toward the horizon sky colour for aerial perspective. (c) 15k dust-mote instances drifting via an animated noise offset.

7) SWEEP AND SUN. A large bent plane (L-profile with a 60 cm bevel radius) with an emission gradient by Z (apricot, rose, orchid, violet) and faint noise. The 'sun' is an emissive disc (r = 8, strength about 30) set low in the gradient. Its housing (torus ring, yoke, stand) is built from cylinders in matte graphite metal and stays in silhouette until shot 4. The actual lighting comes from a Sun lamp aligned to the disc, plus area lights.

8) DRUM. A cylinder with solidify (0.3 wall), a rolled lip and bevels, in satin navy anodized metal (metallic 1, roughness 0.35, fine brushed bump), with a faint etched 'RANGE 288'.

9) DESK AND PAPER. Desk: a Poly Haven light wood or laminate PBR at 2K (for example wood_table_001; check the slug via the API). Paper: a procedural tooth (noise plus stretched Voronoi fibres) on a dense, subdivided local patch of about 1.5M verts used only in shot 6; the rest of the sheet is low-res. HDRI: Poly Haven studio_small_09 (or a similar studio HDRI) at low strength, for reflections only.

10) STROKE. Python ray-samples the shot-1 skyline (the maximum silhouette height across the frame), turns it into a 2D polyline, and maps it onto the paper as a curve. A GN node on the paper patch computes Geometry Proximity to the curve, then stroke = smoothstep(width - distance) * (curve parameter at or below 'progress') * tooth_height_mask. The shader mixes in crimson waxy pigment. The hero tip follows the curve with a Follow Path constraint, and progress is keyed to it.

11) TITLE. A text object using a free OFL font or a system sans, converted to mesh and used as a displacement stamp into the paper, with the emboss factor keyed on the final hit.

12) ANIMATION. All keyframes are written by Python with explicit Bezier handles (an exponential curve for the shot 4 pull-back), Noise F-modifiers for the tremor, and beat_pulse keyed from a beats.json produced by numpy onset/beat analysis of the chosen music WAV.

13) RENDER. EEVEE at 2560x1440. Raytracing uses screen tracing at 1/2 resolution with fast GI. Virtual shadow maps are high-res. TAA uses 64 samples (96 in shots 1 to 3 for the volume), film filter 1.5, motion blur on. Volume tile size 8 with 64 steps, restricted to the slab bounds. Each shot is its own camera and frame range, rendered to its own folder as 16-bit PNG. Compositor: Glare (bloom), Lens Distortion with dispersion about 0.004, vignette.

14) ASSEMBLY. ffmpeg concatenates the sequences at 24 fps, adds light grain (noise filter), and encodes H.265 10-bit plus an H.264 high-bitrate master. The audio mix (adelay, volume, afade, amix, loudnorm to -14 LUFS) is muxed in.
concepts.detail_strategy:
The film relies on true-to-life micro craft on one object type repeated 288 times, which an AI can build very precisely, instead of many half-finished models.

1) Every pencil has the real physical layers: lacquer with clearcoat orange-peel, a thin white primer seam at the scalloped edge, cedar wood with procedural growth rings and longitudinal fibres, sharpener-blade facet ridges, chip-outs, and a pigment core with crystalline sparkle. Tips vary: sharp, blunt, broken.
2) Close-ups hold up: the hero has embossed silver-foil lettering and a dipped end cap, and there are 6 stamped variants for the others. All edges are bevelled, with no razor CG edges anywhere.
3) Scale-ambiguous detail fills the frame: GN-scattered crumbs and shaving curls that read as boulders and debris, plus 15k dust motes as haze.
4) Lighting and lens choices sell the scale. Shots 1 to 3 use hard low sun, deep focus, mist and wide lenses, which reads as kilometres. Shots 4 to 6 switch to studio softboxes, shallow DOF and long lenses, which reads as centimetres. The change of DOF is itself the storytelling tool.
5) Colour is disciplined: 24 saturated pigments set against neutral wood and paper and a dark navy drum, so the colours pop instead of fighting. AgX Punchy keeps the saturation from clipping.
6) Compositing finish: bloom on the sun and highlights, slight dispersion, vignette, fine grain in the encode, 16-bit frames to avoid banding in the gradient sky, and 2560x1440 output.
7) Test renders of a single frame per shot are reviewed by eye and fixed before the overnight render: illusion strength in shots 1 and 2, legibility of the lettering in shot 3, and readability of the pull-back in shot 4.
concepts.risks:
1) LAPTOP SAFETY (the user's explicit request). Before every Blender launch, check for other running Blender processes and free RAM. If another Blender job is running, queue and wait rather than run in parallel. Only one render process at a time, at BelowNormal priority (start /belownormal), capped at -t 8 threads, leaving headroom for other jobs and the OS. Keep the scene under about 6 to 8 GB (2K textures at most, instancing instead of realized geometry, the dense paper patch only in shot 6). Render frame-by-frame image sequences with use_overwrite=False and use_placeholder=True into a unique output folder, so a crash loses at most one frame and never touches another job's files. Write no huge sims, and no Python loops that create thousands of objects. Run test renders at 25 to 50% resolution first.

2) RENDER TIME. The estimate is about 20 to 30 s per frame at 1440p, so about 4 to 6 hours for 720 frames. Benchmark one frame per shot first. If a shot goes over 35 s per frame: lower TAA to 32 to 48, set raytracing to 1/4 resolution, raise volume tile size to 16, or swap the volume slab for 3 to 4 layered noise alpha cards. Render at 4K only if the test averages under about 25 s per frame, otherwise stay at 2560x1440.

3) THE ILLUSION BREAKS TOO EARLY (a symmetrical cone looks like a pencil). The cloud slab hides every painted hex body, tips are varied, worn and chipped, deep focus, mist and wide lenses are used, and the camera never gets a top-down view before shot 4. Hero peaks are framed off-axis so their perfect symmetry is not obvious.

4) VOLUME FLICKER OR COST. Keep the volume bounded to a thin slab with stable seeds and enough samples, with the alpha-card fallback above.

5) THE INSTANCER COLOUR ATTRIBUTE NOT READING IN EEVEE. Fall back to Object Info Random into a constant Color Ramp.

6) SHIMMER AND ALIASING on wood grain and paper tooth at distance. Fade bump strength by camera distance, use the LOD switch, and keep a 1.5 filter.

7) FAST PULL-BACK SMEAR AND JUDDER in shot 4. Use the exponential distance curve, motion blur steps of 1 to 2, and check a 48-frame proxy.

8) INTERPENETRATION when the hero pencil lifts or neighbours dance. Use a 0.2 mm packing gap, translation along Z only, and a lift path on the exact axis.

9) STROKE GN COST. Proximity is computed only on the local patch; if it is slow, bake progress per frame to an attribute cache.

10) AUDIO SYNC. Derive beats.json from the actual edited music WAV and key beat_pulse from it, so picture and sound stay locked.
concepts.audio_plan:
MUSIC: one real royalty-free track (Pixabay Music, Mixkit, or incompetech CC-BY with credit), about 120 BPM so that one beat equals 12 frames. It needs an airy or atmospheric intro, a rising tension section, a clean stop or break, and a punchy percussive or hybrid-electronic groove with big drums and playful plucks or pizzicato. Mood arc: wonder, then tension, then euphoric play. Search terms: 'cinematic hybrid trailer 120 bpm', 'epic electronic build up drop', 'cinematic percussion playful', 'inspiring future bass cinematic'.

Edit (cutting and fading the real recording only, no synthesis): put the track's drop exactly at 20.5 s, use its ambient intro for 0 to 9.5 s, let the riser climb through 9.5 to 14.0 s, open a half-beat gap at 14.5 s, land a hit on the 15.0 s cut, and end on a button or final hit at about 29.3 s with a natural tail to 30.0 s. Run numpy onset/beat detection on the final edit to produce beats.json, which drives the pencil wave.

SFX (Pixabay SFX, Mixkit, Freesound CC0, OpenGameArt CC0; log licences in credits.txt):
- 0.0 to 9.5 s: high mountain wind ambience at low level.
- 0.0 to 9.5 s: a faint deep earth drone.
- 10.2 s: rock tremor or earth rumble.
- 10.8 to 14.0 s: a slow wooden creak or friction groan, pitch-shifted down for scale, layered with stone grinding.
- 11.0 to 13.0 s: a gravel or small-rocks trickle for the falling crumbs.
- 13.2 s: a rising whoosh as the camera tilts.
- 15.0 s: a cinematic sub boom or impact on the cut.
- 15.0 to 20.0 s: a long reverse whoosh or air rush for the pull-back.
- About 18.5 s: a faint electrical hum of a studio light as the LED panel is revealed.
- 20.5 to 25.5 s: pencils or wooden sticks clattering in a cup, cut onto the downbeats; a big clatter or slam at the 24.9 s unison leap.
- 26.3 s: a pencil tap on paper.
- 26.4 to 28.5 s: a pencil scratching or writing on paper.
- 29.3 s: a soft paper press or deep thud for the emboss, under the music button.

Mix in ffmpeg with adelay and volume, with music ducked about 3 dB under the uproot SFX, and loudnorm to -14 LUFS integrated with a -1 dBTP ceiling.

concepts.title: FLIPSIDE
concepts.logline: A close-up of glossy tangerine sequins pulls out to show they cover an entire desert. One racing flip-wave turns that desert into a liquid cobalt ocean. A sea cliff then breaks apart into a glittering murmuration (a swirling flock) of tiles, which lands and builds a blossoming magenta jacaranda grove. Finally the whole world is revealed as a tiny sequin planet that opens a giant eye, blinks at us, and shrinks back into the sequin we started on, so the 30 s film loops seamlessly.
concepts.surprise:
Every surprise comes from the same object, a hexagonal sequin with a centre hole and a different colour on each side. Because of that, each twist feels impossible when it happens and obvious afterwards.

1) Scale reveal, 3.5-6.0 s (S2). The opening shot looks like abstract glitter. The camera crane rises without a cut and shows that the sequins are the skin of a desert a kilometre wide: the dunes, quiver trees and cliff are all made of them.

2) The ground turns to liquid, 8.5 s (S3), on the music drop. The cobalt flip-front passes under the camera. It does more than recolour the ground: about 0.4 s behind the colour change, the dunes become rolling ocean swells made of the same tiles. The cobalt metal reflects the sky, so it suddenly reads as water.

3) Rock becomes flock becomes flower, 14.8-19.5 s (S4). The sea cliff peels apart from its summit down. About 180k tiles take off, swarm like starlings over the camera, flip to hot magenta in mid-air, and land to build a hill and five giant jacaranda trees from the ground up, one blossom cluster at a time.

4) The world is alive, 24.5 s (S5). From orbit, flip-waves meet on the ocean side of the planet and paint a giant eye: pearl white, chartreuse iris, indigo pupil. It blinks once, and the pupil turns to look straight into the lens.

5) The infinite loop, 26-30 s (S6). A sun glint flashes to white and we are back in the opening macro framing. The planet is now a bead the size of one sequin, resting among the tiles. The tile next to it flips over the bead like a lid, and the last frame matches frame 0 exactly, which invites a rewatch.

Why it works: each beat breaks a different rule. Scale (glitter becomes landscape), state of matter (solid becomes liquid), inanimate to alive (rock becomes flock becomes forest), and world to object (planet becomes bead).
concepts.palette:
Sequin colour states. Each tile has a different colour on each side, and colours change on flips.
- Tangerine Lacquer #FF5A1F: side A. A glossy dielectric candy coat (clearcoat 1.0, roughness 0.12), deliberately NOT metallic so it never reads as gold.
- Blood Coral #FF2E4D: a hue-jitter partner for side A.
- Cobalt Anodize #1430FF: side B. Metallic 1.0, roughness 0.18, thin-film about 350 nm.
- Ultramarine Deep #0B1A8C: ocean troughs.
- Hot Magenta Pearl #FF1F8F: side C. Metallic 0.8, thin-film about 500 nm.
- Electric Violet #6E2BFF: mixed with magenta in the jacaranda blossoms.
- Acid Chartreuse #B8FF1F: spray tips, sparks and the eye's iris.
- Pearl White #F4F1FF (thin-film about 280 nm): the eye's white and the sequin clouds.
- Ink Indigo #120A2E: the pupil, the space background and the gaps under the tiles.

Sky and light:
- Zenith #1A1046 grading to Apricot Haze #FFB27A at the horizon.
- Sun #FFE3B8, low (6-8 degrees elevation) and raking. This gives long dune shadows and the most specular glints.
- Cool indigo sky fill. Strong backlight for the murmuration. Magenta rim plus hard white-warm key on the planet.

Mood: golden-hour euphoria turning into cosmic wonder.

No teal and no gold anywhere. Tangerine against cobalt is a complementary pair for maximum punch, and magenta, chartreuse and pearl are the accents.

Grading: AgX with the Punchy look (A/B test against Standard so tangerine does not skew toward yellow), plus a slight saturation lift in the compositor.

shots.description: THE SKIN. Extreme macro on shingled, overlapping hexagonal sequins of tangerine candy lacquer, each cupped, with a bevelled edge and a centre hole. They rock gently as if breathing, and glints crawl across them. At 1.8 s one tile flips with a springy overshoot (rotates 188 degrees, settles at 180) to show its anodized cobalt underside. At 2.4 s a line of flips races away from the lens into the bokeh like falling dominoes: something is coming.
shots.camera: 100 mm. f-stop about 0.4 to fake macro depth of field at the 0.36 m tile scale. Slow lateral slide at 0.15 m/s. Focus racks from a foreground tile to the first flipping tile at 1.8 s. Subtle procedural handheld noise (F-curve noise modifier, about 0.2 degrees).
shots.key_elements: LOD0 hero sequin mesh (hole, bevel, cup). About 8k instances. Rocking noise. First flip with spring overshoot. Receding domino flip line. Sun glints with star-streak glare.

shots.description: THE REVEAL. A continuous, accelerating crane-up out of the macro shows the scale. Endless tangerine and coral sequin dunes, with the tiles aligned in fish-scale rows along the wind ripples. Three quiver trees and a tall cliff, all skinned in sequins, glitter under a low apricot sun, and glitter motes drift in the air. On the horizon a cobalt front, topped with glittering spray, crawls toward the camera.
shots.camera: Starts on the S1 lens. Rises from 0.5 m to 70 m altitude in 5 s with an exponential ease-in. Pitches from looking down to looking forward. Zooms 100 to 32 mm at the same time (a partial dolly-zoom that exaggerates scale). The f-stop opens up to f/5.6 by the end.
shots.key_elements: Dune heightfield. Poly Haven quiver trees and cliff, used only as surfaces to sample sequin positions. About 350k near instances plus a shader-faked far field. Light world-volume haze. Cobalt front and spray on the horizon. About 3k air motes.

shots.description: THE FRONT, landing on the music drop. The camera rides WITH the flip-front at about 25 m/s, looking along its line, so the frame splits. Left: tangerine dunes. Right: cobalt ocean swells made of the same tiles. The front is a rolling bulge of flipping tiles, and chartreuse and pearl sequin spray is thrown 2-5 m high. Glints sweep across the frame as the tiles change angle. At 12.0 s a whip-pan of 150 degrees right faces the new ocean. A 6 m swell of tiles rises toward the lens and crashes in a burst of sequin spray that fills the frame, which is where the cut happens.
shots.camera: 24 mm, f/4, 1.8 m above the tiles, tracking parallel to the front so it stays a vanishing line just right of centre. Procedural shake tied to the front. Motion blur shutter 0.5. The whip-pan is an eased 8-frame yaw, smeared by motion blur.
shots.key_elements: Flip spring. Height change from dunes to ocean lagging the colour by 0.4 s. Gerstner-like swells. Analytic (formula-driven) ballistic spray, about 30k. The hero swell crash. Composition split desert/ocean.

shots.description: MURMURATION. A low-angle shot of the towering sea cliff, now cobalt, rising from the swells with the dusk sun behind it. At 14.8 s the cliff peels from the summit down. Tiles lift off in sheets, tumbling, and gather into a dense, shape-shifting murmuration of about 180k glittering tiles that swirl against the apricot-to-indigo sky. A wave travels through the flock flipping every tile to hot magenta. At 17.5 s the flock dives over the camera. The camera turns to follow as the flock spirals down and lands, building a hill and then five giant jacaranda trees from the ground up, their blossoms forming as dense magenta and violet sequin clusters. The shot ends on the backlit hero tree with star glints.
shots.camera: Starts at 50 mm, tilting up to follow the lift-off. During the overhead dive the lens animates 50 to 18 mm with a 15 degree roll, then a 120 degree pan follows the descent. Settles into a slow push-in on the hero tree at 35 mm, f/2.8.
shots.key_elements: Sequin-skinned cliff surface. Flock animated by formulas, with no physics simulation. The flock centre follows a Bezier path, and each tile keeps its own position inside an ellipsoid that breathes with noise. Magenta flip wave through the flock. Landing targets sampled from a hill and Poly Haven jacaranda_tree meshes, built from the ground up. Backlight with streak glints.

shots.description: THE WINK. Cut to inside the hero canopy. The camera rockets straight up through drifting clouds of pearl sequin clusters. The horizon bends, and we see a small planet completely skinned in sequins, with three zones: tangerine desert, cobalt ocean and magenta forest. It has a fresnel atmosphere glow (brighter at the edges) and sits against a deep indigo star field. Flip-fronts race around the globe. At 23.5 s they meet on the ocean face and paint a giant eye: pearl white, chartreuse iris, indigo pupil. At 24.5 s it blinks once, with the eyelids sweeping as flip-waves, and the pupil turns toward the lens. At 25.6 s one sequin catches the sun and a starburst glint floods the frame to white.
shots.camera: 35 mm. Exponential vertical pull from 0 to 3 km (in the planet scene's scale). Orbits 20 degrees while pulling back, and the roll settles to level. The cut from the canopy is a match on upward motion.
shots.key_elements: Separate planet scene with about 250k larger tiles (1.4 m) plus shader-faked far sequins. Biome mask. Flip-fronts as spherical caps. Procedural eye mask with blink and look. Fresnel atmosphere shell. Sequin clouds (15 clusters x 1.5k). Glint to white flash.

shots.description: THE LID (loop). Out of the white comes the exact framing of S1: a macro of tangerine tiles. Now a bead the size of one sequin rests among them: the planet, tiny, with all three zones, slowly spinning. A ring of cobalt flips ripples outward from it and settles back to tangerine. At 28.6 s the neighbouring tile flips over the bead like a lid, hiding it. The tiles settle, and at 30.0 s the frame is identical to frame 0.
shots.camera: Same 100 mm, f-stop 0.4 and slide direction as S1. The path is built so its final pose and focus distance exactly equal S1's frame-0 pose. Exposure decays from white over the first 6 frames.
shots.key_elements: Duplicate of the S1 scene. Bead made of a displaced icosphere with the sequin shader, carrying the three biomes. Outward ring of flips. Lid flip. Last frame equals first frame for a seamless loop.

concepts.build_plan:
A. Pipeline (headless bpy, Blender 5.2)
- common.py holds:
  - the sequin meshes and materials
  - the node groups
  - a height-function library
  - render and compositor setup
  - a property-introspection helper that checks the 5.2 EEVEE property names with dir() before setting them
- shot1.py to shot6.py each build one .blend with its own scene, camera and animation.
- Each shot renders separately: `blender -b shotN.blend -t 6 -a`, written to PNG 16-bit sequences with Overwrite off and Placeholders on, so renders can resume.
- assemble.py builds the edit in the Video Sequencer: 6 image strips plus music and SFX strips with volume keyframes. It exports an H.264 MP4 (high bitrate, AAC 320k) and keeps the PNG master.

B. The sequin mesh (bmesh)
- LOD0, the near version:
  - a 6-sided cylinder, radius 0.18 m, depth 0.01
  - top and bottom faces inset 0.8, centre faces deleted and bridged to make a 3.5 cm centre hole
  - cupped by z += 0.025*(r/R)^2
  - a 4 mm bevel with 1 segment, weighted normals, smooth shading
  - material slot 0 = Top, slot 1 = Under
- LOD1, beyond 25 m: a flat hexagon n-gon. Its shader uses the Backfacing input to pick the side, so it stays two-coloured at about 12 tris.

C. Point sets, built in numpy rather than Distribute Points, so they stay stable
- Ground points:
  - a hex lattice with 0.32 m spacing (about 12% overlap gives the shingled fish-scale look) and 2% jitter
  - stored attributes: rest (float3), id, rnd, arrival time, lod
  - arrival time = dot(rest.xy, front_dir)/25 m/s + noise(rest*0.02)*1.2 + rnd*0.08
- Points on asset surfaces:
  - sampled area-weighted from the triangles of the Poly Haven meshes (quiver_tree_01/02, a namaqualand_cliff_* or coastal_cliff_* chosen via the API, 2 namaqualand boulders, jacaranda_tree)
  - thinned to Poisson-like spacing with grid hashing, normals stored
  - the asset meshes themselves are hidden from render
- Static frustum cull per shot:
  - sample the shot camera every 4 frames
  - project all points with vectorized camera matrices and keep any point visible in any sample, with a 10% margin
  - the point count stays constant for the whole shot, which gives stable IDs and motion vectors, so EEVEE motion blur works and nothing pops
- Each result is written as a vertex-only mesh object carrying those attributes.

D. Geometry Nodes group 'SequinSkin', applied to each point mesh
- t = Scene Time.
- flip = FloatCurve(clamp((t - arrival)/0.32)), a spring shape: 0, 1.08, 0.97, 1.
- morph = smoothstep(clamp((t - arrival - 0.4)/0.8)).
- height = mix(Dunes(rest), Ocean(rest, t), morph).
  - Dunes: a ridged, domain-warped sine, (1-|sin(k*(x+warp))|)^1.5, plus large-scale 4D noise.
  - Ocean: 4 directional Gerstner-like sines with horizontal displacement, plus a fine noise chop.
- Normal: central differences, evaluating the height group at rest +/- epsilon.
- Set Position: rest plus height, plus a lift of sin(pi*flip)*0.12 along the normal.
- Rotation:
  - Align Rotation to Vector(normal), oriented along the wind direction
  - then a local-X rotation of pi*flip, plus an 8 degree shingle tilt, plus 4 degrees of noise rocking
- Instance on Points: LOD0 and LOD1 as two branches split by the lod attribute.
- Store Named Attribute 'stage' and 'jit' on the instance domain. Shaders read them with Attribute nodes set to Instancer.
- Never Realize Instances.

E. Materials
- 'Sequin_Top' and 'Sequin_Under' map 'stage' to colour states: 0 tangerine lacquer, 1 cobalt anodize, 2 magenta pearl, 3 pearl, 4 chartreuse, 5 indigo ink.
- Thin film comes from the Principled BSDF. If 5.2 EEVEE ignores it, fall back to a Layer Weight-driven colour ramp.
- Per-instance hue jitter of +/-3% and roughness jitter of +/-0.06.
- A radial Wave-texture micro-bump of concentric stamped rings, strength 0.05, produces star-shaped glints.
- A deep coral and indigo 'Underlay' ground mesh shows through the holes and gaps.
- A stage swap happens only while a face is pointing down, so a 3-state colour chain (tangerine to cobalt to magenta) is possible with 2 physical sides.

F. Far field
- A 600x600 grid displaced by the same height functions in Geometry Nodes.
- Shader-only sequins:
  - Voronoi cells sized at 1/tile
  - per-cell random normal tilt plus a dome bump
  - colour taken from the same front function, computed from object position and a 'time' value driven by #frame/24
- Fades into the near instances inside haze and depth of field.

G. Spray and motes
- Spray: 30k points with birth times spread along the front. Position = p0 + v*a + 0.5*g*a^2, where a = t - birth. Visible while 0 < a < 1.3 s, scaled out, tumbling.
- Motes: 3k tiles drifting on 4D noise and flipping slowly, so they catch glints.

H. Murmuration (formula-driven, no simulation)
- Sources: about 180k cliff samples, sorted by height, highest first.
- Targets: samples from the hill plus 5 jacaranda trees (foliage weighted x3), sorted by height, lowest first, and matched to sources by rank.
- The flock centre follows a Python-defined Bezier path that passes over the camera and spirals into the grove.
- Each tile has its own offset inside an ellipsoid. The ellipsoid is stretched and twisted by 4D noise so the flock breathes like starlings.
- Three overlapping phases mixed with smoothsteps:
  - lift: source to flock slot, with launch delay = rank*1.5 s + rnd*0.2
  - fly: Sample Curve at factor(t) plus the local offset
  - land: flock slot to target, staggered by rank so the grove builds from the ground up
- While flying, tiles tumble about a random axis at 3 rev/s, then blend into the landing normal.
- The magenta flip wave is driven by the local offset x plus time.

I. Planet scene
- 250k Fibonacci-sphere points on a 180 m radius planet with 1.4 m tiles.
- A 3D noise biome mask with heights per biome.
- Flip-fronts are spherical caps that spread from 3 seed points at a set angular speed.
- Eye mask in the tangent frame of the camera-facing point:
  - eyelids: |v| < open(t)*(1-u^2)^0.8
  - iris radius 0.38, pupil radius 0.16, offset by a keyed look vector
  - blink keyed at 24.5 s
- Atmosphere: a shell at R*1.04 with Layer Weight fresnel emission, apricot to magenta, blended as transparent.
- Background: indigo gradient plus Voronoi star specks.
- Sequin clouds: 15 instanced clusters.

J. World and light
- A Poly Haven low-sun pure-sky HDRI (2k; search 'puresky' plus 'sunset' or 'dawn' via the API) lights the scene and feeds reflections only.
- Camera rays see a procedural gradient sky instead, switched with the Is Camera Ray output of the Light Path node.
- Sun lamp: angle 0.5 degrees, strength 5, #FFE3B8.
- World volume at density 0.002 in S2-S4 only, with volumetric tile size 16.

K. Render settings
- EEVEE, 2560x1440, 24 fps, 720 frames.
- Samples: 64 (96 for S1 and S6).
- Raytracing: screen-trace with light-probe fallback, denoise on, fast GI.
- Shadows: virtual shadow maps, 1 ray, 6 steps.
- Motion blur: shutter 0.5, 1 step (2 for S4).
- Film filter 1.5 px.

L. Compositor
- Glare Streaks: 4 streaks, high threshold, so sequins throw star-filter glints.
- A subtle Glare bloom.
- Lens Distortion dispersion 0.008.
- Ellipse-mask vignette.
- The S3 whip, the S5 white flash and the S6 fade-in from white are all done inside the renders, matched across the cut.

M. Look-dev loop
- For each shot: render 5 key frames at 50% resolution and inspect them.
- Then render a 24-frame strip at 50% to check for shimmer.
- Then 1 full-resolution frame to measure time and RAM.
concepts.detail_strategy:
Detail is layered across four scales, and every scale comes from the same sequin, so the image stays dense without becoming messy.

1) Micro, the sequin itself:
- centre hole, cupped dish and bevelled rim that catches edge highlights
- stamped concentric-ring micro-bump that throws star-shaped glints
- thin-film iridescence on the metal sides
- a different finish on each side, so flips change both colour and reflection
- per-tile hue and roughness jitter so no two tiles are identical

2) Meso, how tiles sit together:
- an ordered, shingled hex lattice (fish scales) that bends over the terrain and lines up with the wind ripples. Order looks premium; random scatter looks cheap.
- 8 degree overlap tilt and breathing rocking noise
- a dark underlay showing through the holes, which adds depth

3) Macro, the forms:
- crisp dune ridges, Gerstner swells, the cliff and quiver-tree silhouettes
- the jacaranda canopies, whose blossom clusters are dense sequin clumps

4) Atmosphere:
- glitter motes and spray catching the low sun
- light aerial haze, the fresnel atmosphere around the planet, sequin clouds for parallax

Animated detail adds richness without adding geometry. Moving flip-fronts mean glints are always sweeping across surfaces, and the spring overshoot plus tiny per-tile timing offsets give every front texture. Composition is graphic and clean: every frame has 1-2 dominant colour fields (tangerine against cobalt, magenta against indigo) with a saturated accent, so it reads like a motion-design studio piece rather than noise.

Cleanliness:
- EEVEE at 64-96 samples with a 1.5 px filter
- roughness never below 0.12, which prevents firefly glints
- frustum culling keeps every visible tile real geometry while the far field fades into a matched shader
- near-zero volumetrics, so there is no grain
- a compositor star-glare pass for the jewellery-commercial sparkle
- final at 2560x1440 native
concepts.risks:
SYSTEM SAFETY (the user explicitly asked not to crash the laptop and said other Blender jobs may be running):
- Before every build, test or final render, check for running blender.exe processes and free RAM. Never run more than one Blender process from this pipeline, and wait or queue whenever another heavy Blender job is active. The 780M shares system RAM, and GPU contention can cause driver timeout resets (TDR crashes).
- Cap threads with -t 6 (of 16) and launch at BelowNormal priority so the machine stays responsive.
- Memory budget of 10 GB or less per shot, counting iGPU shared memory. Measure peak RAM in a 1-frame test. A watchdog pauses between chunks if free RAM drops below about 12 GB.
- Never Realize Instances. Keep textures and HDRIs at 1-2k. No fluid, particle or cloth bakes and no high-resolution volumes.
- Render in resumable chunks of about 50 frames (Overwrite off plus Placeholders), so an interruption costs at most one frame. Allow brief thermal cool-downs between chunks.
- Download assets and audio into their own isolated folders.

QUALITY AND RENDER RISKS:
1) Sub-pixel specular shimmer and flicker from millions of tiny mirrors. This is the biggest risk. Mitigations:
- keep tiles at 8 px or more on screen near camera (tile size is set per scene; the planet uses 1.4 m tiles)
- roughness floor of 0.12
- 64-96 samples and a 1.5 px filter
- motion blur
- the far field is shader-faked and slightly softened by haze and depth of field
- check a 24-frame strip at 50% before committing
2) Instance load and render time. Expected: about 8k (S1 and S6), 350k (S2), 330k (S3), 400k (S4) and 250k (S5) instances, with LOD1 at about 12 tris beyond 25 m, so roughly 4-8M tris per frame. Estimated per frame at 1440p: S1/S6 about 15 s, S2/S3 about 30 s, S4 about 35 s, S5 about 25 s, about 5.3 h in total. If a test frame goes over 40 s, cut far-instance density and lower samples to 48 before lowering resolution. 4K only if the measured average is under 25 s per frame (it probably won't be).
3) Motion-blur artefacts when the point count changes. Prevented by fixed per-shot point sets with stable IDs and by never deleting points mid-shot (hide them by scaling to 0 instead).
4) Blender 5.2 API drift: EEVEE property names, Glare node types, thin-film support. Introspect with dir() in a 10-second headless probe first. Fallbacks: a Layer Weight fake iridescence, and a Glare Fog Glow plus streaks setup.
5) The tangerine side reading as gold under warm light. It is a dielectric lacquer, pushed red-orange (#FF5A1F), and kept away from the low-sun specular colour.
6) The murmuration reading as a blob or as noise. Keep a strong silhouette with an ellipsoid that breathes like starlings, high contrast against the sky, and tumble rates chosen to spread glints. Review 5 frames from different angles.
7) The eye reading as cheesy. Build it from clean geometric arcs and test. Fallback: a giant chartreuse spiral that winks.
8) Match cuts (S5 to S6 and the loop). S6's camera path is solved backwards from S1's frame 0, and the white flash hides the scale jump. Verify frame 720 against frame 0 with a difference image.
9) Two-tone sequins reading as roof tiles. The hexagon, centre hole, cup, metallic sheen and flips make them read unmistakably as sequins.
concepts.audio_plan:
MUSIC
Sources, all real recordings, nothing synthesized: Pixabay Music (Pixabay licence), Mixkit (free licence), freepd (CC0), or incompetech (CC BY 4.0, credit required). Keep a LICENSES.txt with URLs and credits.

Mood: playful and glassy wonder that builds into a euphoric drop, an airy floating breakdown, then a cosmic swell and a ringing tail. Genre: cinematic future-bass or hybrid electronic with orchestral swells, plus mallet, celesta or glass-pluck textures that match the glitter. Tempo 120-128 BPM; at 120 BPM a beat is exactly 12 frames.

Search terms: 'future bass cinematic', 'epic electronic trailer', 'glitch orchestral build drop', 'magical electronic sparkle'.

Edit in the Video Sequencer:
- Place a downbeat at 0.5 s, so bars fall every 2.0 s.
- The drop lands at 8.5 s (S3), the pull-out riser starts at 20.5 s, and the big hit is at 24.5 s (the blink).
- Shift cuts by up to 6 frames to match the real track's downbeats.
- Splice at bar boundaries with 50 ms crossfades.
- Fade the tail so the end loops back into the opening tick.
