concepts.title: ONESIDE
concepts.logline: A persimmon-red maglev rides a world that has only one side: a huge twisted Möbius ribbon of coral canyons, magenta forests and cobalt rivers floating in a violet void. Gravity always points into the ground wherever you stand. Sunset happens when the land itself rolls over, and rivers pour around the rim of the world instead of off it. The 30-second film loops seamlessly, so like its world it never ends.
concepts.surprise:
1) 0:03-0:04.5, THE SKY IS LAND. The camera cranes up out of a sunny meadow and the horizon does not end. The land curves up into a giant arch, and directly overhead hangs the far side of the world, upside down: a night landscape dotted with tangerine lantern lights, seen through a blue noon haze. Viewers first think they are looking at a normal valley, then realise the sky is made of land.
2) 0:06-0:09, THE TURN. The camera is locked level with the speeding train. As the ribbon enters its corkscrew, the whole world (mesas, forests, sky and sun) rolls 180 degrees around the steady train in 3 seconds. The sun sets under the ground and a razor-sharp shadow line sweeps across the canyon like a clock hand. Sunset is caused by the ground turning its back on the sun, not by time passing.
3) 0:12.8-0:14.6, OVER THE RIM. A glowing night river pours off the edge of the world. The camera follows it over, expecting a fall into the void, but the water curls tightly around the 24 m thick striped rim. The camera curls with it, upside down, and comes up on the other face of the same spot in blinding noon sun. Midnight to noon in 1.8 seconds, and gravity turns over with the camera.
4) 0:15.5-0:22.5, THE REVEAL. A 5 km pull-out shows the whole world: one colossal Möbius ribbon, half blazing with daylight and half glittering with night lanterns, with the day/night line running across its twist. The train is a tiny orange spark on it. This makes sense of everything before it: on this world day and night are places, not times.
5) 0:30 to 0:00, THE LOOP. The final dive lands at the exact pose, speed and focus of frame 1, so the film loops with no visible seam. It is one-sided and endless, like its world, and looks good on repeat on social media.
concepts.palette:
DAY FACE: Chartreuse Meadow #B8F02A; Coral Sandstone #FF6B5B to Vermilion #E8483B (terraced mesas); Hot Magenta Blossom #FF2E9A (jacaranda canopies recoloured); Cobalt River #2457FF; Cream Strata #FFE9C7 (paths and rock bands); Day Sky #3D7BFF fading to #9CC2FF at the horizon.
HERO OBJECT: Persimmon Lacquer #FF5A1F (maglev, clearcoat); Porcelain White #F4F1EC (rail and pylons); Smoked Glass #1A1420 with Warm Window #FFD9A8 emission.
NIGHT FACE: Ultramarine Moss #2A1BFF to Deep Indigo #120A4A; Electric Violet #8A2BFF (ferns and river glow); Sodium Tangerine #FF8A1F and Hot Magenta #FF2E9A lantern pods; firefly specks #FFF0B0.
RIM STRATA ('layer cake' cross-section): Coral #FF6B5B / Cream #FFE9C7 / Plum #6B1F5C / Ultramarine #2A1BFF / Vermilion #E8483B bands.
VOID: Space #0B0726 with an Ultramarine #1B1060 gradient and a Magenta Nebula band #C2189B at 20-35% intensity; the star is white-hot #FFF6E6.
No teal and no gold anywhere: water is cobalt-blue, never turquoise, and warm accents are persimmon or tangerine, never metallic gold.
LIGHTING MOOD: one hard white-hot sun (Sun lamp, angle 0.4 degrees for crisp, graphic shadows) plus a coloured world fill. The day face is high-key and very saturated, with crisp shadows and blue aerial haze. The night face is dark violet ambient punctuated by small warm practical lights (emission plus small point lights). AgX view with the 'Punchy' look, then compositor saturation and contrast to taste. Bloom on the star, lanterns and train windows only.

shots.description: NOON MEADOW / THE SKY IS LAND (frames 1-108). Opens at grass-blade height in a chartreuse meadow dense with coral gazania and cream ursinia flowers; pollen motes drift slowly UPWARD, the first subtle wrong-physics hint. At 2.2 s the persimmon maglev slices overhead on its porcelain rail 8 m up, with a whoosh. The camera cranes up after it, tilting from level to about 38 degrees up. This reveals the valley (coral terraced mesas topped with alien quiver trees, magenta jacaranda groves, a winding cobalt river) and then the punchline: the land rises into a vast arch across the sky. Straight overhead, softened by blue haze, hangs the dark underside of the far side of the world, upside down and sprinkled with tangerine lantern lights.
shots.camera: 24 mm. Starts 0.35 m above the ground moving forward at 6 m/s (this exact pose and speed is also the last frame of the film, for the loop). f/2.0 focused at 1.2 m on the flower heads, racking to infinity from 2.0 to 3.0 s as the train passes. Crane up to 35 m by 4.5 s with ease-in-out, tilt 0 to +38 degrees, slight 5 degree yaw to follow the train. Motion blur shutter 0.5.
shots.key_elements: Procedural GN grass blades only within a 30 m corridor around the baked camera path (about 1.5-2M instances, never realized); Poly Haven gazania, ursinia, grass clumps and shrubs recoloured to the palette; jacaranda_tree with magenta blossom tint; quiver trees on the mesas; the maglev and rail; the overhead arch (low-res global ribbon plus lantern instances); mist-pass aerial perspective; pollen GN points drifting along the surface normal.

shots.description: THE TURN, a corkscrew sunset (frames 109-240). Hard cut on the musical downbeat to a flank tracking chase. The camera is locked to the maglev's own frame: the train stays sharp and steady while the landscape streaks past. The ribbon enters the Corkscrew, a 180 degree twist over 320 m. Because the camera's horizon is locked to the train, the whole world rolls around it from 6.0 to 9.0 s: mesas swing overhead, the sky rotates under the train, and the sun slides down and sets UNDER the ground. A razor-sharp shadow terminator sweeps across the canyon like a clock hand. The colour goes from white noon to tangerine to violet night, and at 8.8 s the train's window strips flicker on, warm white, in three quick stutters.
shots.camera: 35 mm. Rig parented to the lead car's baked frame: offset 14 m to the side, 3 m up, 6 m ahead, looking back at about 25 degrees for a 3/4 view of the train. Zero roll relative to the train, so the world does the rolling. Train speed 60 m/s, so pylons every 30 m flick past at about 2 per second for rhythm. f/4 focused on the lead car's nose. Motion blur 0.5 smears the foreground terrain.
shots.key_elements: Corkscrew section of the ribbon at full hero resolution along the rail; fixed Sun lamp (the rig really rotates through world space, so the lighting change is physically correct and free); world colour and sky gradient keyframed from day to night in sync with dot(surface normal, sun direction) sampled at the train; emission keyframes on the train windows; porcelain pylons; jacaranda and quiver silhouettes rolling across the sun disk for a starburst glint.

shots.description: NIGHT SIDE, THEN OVER THE RIM (frames 241-372). On the night face a bioluminescent forest of violet ferns, ultramarine moss, blue heliophila and arching GN 'lantern pod' stems tipped with tangerine and magenta glowing bulbs, with fireflies drifting. The river glows violet-cobalt. The camera glides low over the river toward the edge of the world, where the water pours over the rim. At 12.8 s the camera follows it over and pitches down 90 degrees. The rim cross-section fills the frame: a 24 m thick striped 'layer cake' of coral, cream, plum and ultramarine strata. The water does NOT fall into the void. It curls tightly around the rim like a ribbon around a table edge, and the camera curls with it through 180 degrees. At 14.6 s it surfaces on the opposite face of the same spot, in full noon sun, and the glare blasts almost to white (this hides the cut).
shots.camera: 18 mm. 1.6 m above the water at 14 m/s with a gentle lateral S-curve, f/2.8, lantern bokeh in the foreground. Rim wrap: the camera rotates about the rim's axis 180 degrees in 1.8 s with smootherstep easing, staying 4 m from the water surface. Exposure keyframed +1.3 EV with a glare ramp over the last 0.6 s for the white-out. Motion blur 0.5.
shots.key_elements: Night flora set (Poly Haven fern, moss and heliophila recoloured, plus procedural lantern pods); about 40 small soft point lights placed at lantern clusters near the path only; rim strata shader on the slab edge; the rim-wrap water ribbon (curve-to-mesh, flowing streak shader, foam emission at the edges); a GN spray-point mist cloud at the wrap; sun glare in the compositor.

shots.description: REVEAL: THE ONE-SIDED WORLD (frames 373-540). Out of the white-out the camera, still at the sunlit rim with the wrapping waterfall in frame, rockets backward and keeps going. It pulls out from 30 m to 5.5 km while orbiting about 50 degrees, revealing the entire world: one colossal twisted Möbius ribbon about 1.3 km across, hanging in an ultramarine void with a magenta nebula band and a single white star. The terminator runs diagonally through the corkscrew. One stretch of the ribbon blazes with coral, chartreuse and magenta daylight, while the other glitters with thousands of tangerine lantern pinpricks on deep indigo. Thin white waterfall threads wrap around the rim at four points. The maglev is a single persimmon spark crawling along the band. A tilted ring of about 3000 tumbling boulders orbits the ribbon like a moon belt. The full composition holds from 20.5 s.
shots.camera: Starts at 35 mm and zooms to 50 mm during the pull-out, a slight dolly-zoom compression. Distance interpolated in log space so perceived speed stays even, then ease-out into the hold. f/8, effectively all in focus. Slow 50 degree orbit plus 10 degrees of rise. Final frame: the ribbon on a rule-of-thirds diagonal, the star top-left with glare, the boulder ring crossing the lower foreground.
shots.key_elements: Global ribbon mesh (1.5 m grid) with shader-driven macro colour; sparse tree and lantern instances across the whole ribbon; the S3 hero patch kept in the scene for the first second; world shader (gradient, nebula noise, Voronoi stars); boulder ring; star sphere plus Sun lamp; the train as a small emissive spark mesh; waterfall threads.

shots.description: THE DIVE (frames 541-636). The camera tips forward and dives at the daylight meadow zone, accelerating hard and banking. It threads between tumbling boulders of the ring, with two near-misses (a rock fills half the frame, then doppler whoosh). The ribbon swells to fill the frame, blue haze thickens and mesas and groves resolve. At 26.4 s a large boulder crosses the lens as a full-frame wipe, which hides the cut and the scene swap.
shots.camera: 28 mm on a Bezier dive path, acceleration easing in, up to 20 degrees of bank into the turns that settles to 0 by the wipe. Focus far, motion blur 0.5 for strong streaks on the near boulders. The path is designed so the post-wipe heading matches the S6 heading.
shots.key_elements: Boulder ring (Poly Haven rocks, per-instance spin from ID times frame), global ribbon scene, mist ramp keyed with altitude, one hero wipe boulder animated through the lens.

shots.description: AGAIN, the seamless loop (frames 637-720). Out of the boulder wipe the camera is skimming 12 m over the chartreuse meadow and decelerating. It sinks to grass-blade height, pollen begins to rise, flowers sharpen, and the maglev's hum swells from behind. The final frame matches frame 1's pose, velocity, focus and lighting exactly, so the film loops with no seam and the train is about to pass overhead again.
shots.camera: 24 mm. Descends from 12 m to 0.35 m and decelerates to 6 m/s along a curve built as the time-reversed continuation of S1's first frames, with continuous position and first derivative at the loop point. Rack from infinity to 1.2 m between 28.0 and 29.5 s, f/2.0 at the end, the same exposure as S1.
shots.key_elements: Shares S1's hero meadow .blend and scatter. The loop-matched camera curve is verified by rendering frame 720 and frame 1 side by side and differencing them. The ambience bed is identical to the start.

concepts.build_plan:
ONE SOURCE OF TRUTH: ribbon_core.py defines the world mathematically, and every shot imports it.
1) CENTERLINE AND FRAME. A closed loop of radius 640 m (circumference about 4 km) with three gentle +/-60 m vertical undulations (a 'potato chip', so the pull-out silhouette is elegant rather than a flat ring). frame(s) returns the position C(s), tangent T (finite difference), and a reference normal N0 = radial direction projected perpendicular to T, then rotated about T by the twist angle theta(s). theta(s) is 0 over most of the loop, then a smootherstep 0 to 180 degrees inside the 320 m 'Corkscrew' zone, then 180 degrees until the seam. The seam (where pi wraps back to 0 with the Möbius flip) is placed in a night stretch that no close camera ever visits. map(s, v, h) = C + N*h + B*v gives world position and orientation for any point on the surface. The camera, train, rail, water and scatter all use it, so everything stays in sync with the geometry.
2) SLAB MESH. numpy builds a two-faced slab: face A at h=+12, face B at h=-12 with v mirrored, plus rim walls joining them. Global grid at 1.5 m (about 1.3M quads total). Heights come from a terrain function on the single-surface parameter (periodic 4D mathutils.noise so the A/B surfaces match where they meet at the seam): a meandering river channel (sum of sines), terraced coral mesas near the edges (smoothed quantize of FBM noise to make steps), a raised rim lip, and soft meadow undulation. Mesh attributes stored per vertex: face_id, river_dist, slope, terrace_level, strata_depth, day_factor.
3) HERO PATCHES. Per shot, the same function is resampled at 0.15 m only inside a corridor around that shot's baked camera path. Detail comes from a Displace modifier using a Poly Haven rock or ground displacement map (1K/2K), not from subdivision of the whole ribbon. Each shot is its own scene or .blend containing only its hero patch plus the low-res global ribbon.
4) MATERIALS (procedural colour, Poly Haven detail). The terrain shader mixes by attribute: chartreuse grass (noise-varied hue), coral sandstone (wave texture on height for bands; normal and roughness from a Poly Haven red sandstone or rock texture), cream paths, and on the night face ultramarine moss and violet soil. The rim strata shader is a colour ramp on strata_depth, warped by noise, with a Poly Haven rock_face normal. River: glossy cobalt Principled with an animated noise normal (raytraced reflections); on the night side, a faint violet emission. All Poly Haven models get Hue/Saturation/Value plus a tint mix inserted before Base Color to hit the palette.
5) SCATTER (Geometry Nodes, instances never realized). Distribute Points on Faces (Poisson) with density from attributes multiplied by distance to the shot's whole baked camera path. Scatter is computed once per shot, not per frame, so there is zero popping. Instances use Align Rotation to Vector on the surface normal, because gravity is local: trees grow perpendicular to the ribbon everywhere, including upside down on the arch. Day set: jacaranda (magenta), quiver trees on mesas, tree_small_02, shrubs, gazania/ursinia, grass clumps, boulders, plus procedural GN grass blades (curve-to-mesh blade with a bend) within 30 m of the path. Night set: fern (violet), moss, heliophila, and procedural lantern pods (quadratic Bezier stem plus a UV-sphere bulb, emission 8-20, colour randomised between tangerine and magenta by ID). Fireflies and pollen are GN points with noise offset times frame. The far ribbon gets sparse large trees plus lantern dots only.
6) RAIL AND MAGLEV. The rail curve is generated from map(s, v=-40, h=+20) with per-point tilt matching theta(s). Curve to Mesh with a rounded-rectangle profile, porcelain material. Pylons are instanced every 30 m by GN, with V-shaped struts. The train is 3 cars of 24 m each: a cube with a bevel modifier (3 segments), Subdivision level 2, weighted normals, and nose tapering via simple deform plus a lattice. The window band is a material mask on object Z (smoked glass with animated emissive strips), with a chrome skirt and dark inter-car gaps. Motion: Python bakes a location and quaternion keyframe per frame for each car from map(), with LINEAR interpolation.
7) RIM-WRAP WATER. The curve follows the river centerline to the rim, wraps a semicircle (radius about 13 m) around the slab edge, and continues on the opposite face. Curve to Mesh with a width profile, GN noise displacement, and a shader with flowing streaks (stretched noise and wave textures whose mapping offset is driven by #frame), foam emission at the edges via a curve-param mask, and a slight translucency fake (no refraction). Spray: about 20k GN points around the wrap zone with ID-seeded orbit offsets, rendered as tiny glossy-white spheres with motion blur. Four thin waterfall threads elsewhere on the rim for S4.
8) BOULDER RING. About 3000 instances of 6 Poly Haven rocks in a tilted torus band (GN distribute in volume or a points-on-torus formula), with whole-ring rotation keyframed and per-rock spin = ID hash times frame. One hand-placed hero boulder for the S5 wipe.
9) WORLDS. S4/S5 space world: a gradient plus 4D-noise nebula through a magenta colour ramp plus Voronoi star threshold. A far emissive star sphere aligned with the Sun lamp. Day shots: a cobalt sky gradient with faint stars masked to the zenith. S2: world colours keyframed from day to night in sync with the roll.
10) CAMERAS. Each camera path is defined in ribbon coordinates (s(t), v(t), h(t)) plus look offsets, baked per frame through map() so it hugs the terrain and twist exactly. The S6 end is solved to match the S1 start with C1 continuity.
11) RENDER AND COMPOSITE. EEVEE, 2560x1440, 24 fps, TAA 48-64 samples, raytracing on at half resolution (fast GI / horizon scan), virtual shadows with a capped resolution, no volumetrics, motion blur (shutter 0.5), DOF on, a low-resolution light probe volume bake per shot. Passes: Mist plus Emission. Compositor: mist mixed with a sky-tinted colour for aerial perspective, Glare (Bloom) on emission and the star, mild lens dispersion, vignette, very light grain. Output 16-bit PNG sequences per shot, then an ffmpeg H.265 or H.264 encode (CRF 14) with the mixed audio.
concepts.detail_strategy:
Every frame has detail at three scales, so it reads as dense and premium at both 0.35 m and 5 km:
- MACRO: the impossible silhouette itself (arch overhead, corkscrew, Möbius loop), the day/night terminator as a crisp graphic line, and big flat zones of saturated colour (chartreuse fields, coral mesas, magenta groves, cobalt river) arranged with clear value contrast so they never turn to mush.
- MESO: terraced mesa steps, the meandering river, the rim lip, the 'layer cake' strata on every exposed edge, rows of porcelain pylons, grove clustering (density masks from noise, so it looks designed rather than uniformly sprayed).
- MICRO: millions of GN grass blades and flowers near the lens, Poly Haven normal and roughness detail on all rock, lantern bokeh, pollen and fireflies, spray mist, hard-surface bevels and clearcoat on the train catching sun glints.
Cleanliness: one hard key light, crisp sun shadows, a strictly limited palette (every asset is re-tinted, nothing off-palette), no grunge or dirt maps, AgX Punchy for rich but not clipped saturation, bloom only on true emitters, generous negative space in the void shots. EEVEE gives noise-free frames. Motion blur and DOF give a photographic finish. The train is a fixed scale reference (72 m long), and mist-pass haze sells kilometre-scale depth. Density is spent only where the camera looks: scatter density is driven by distance to each shot's camera path, so close-ups are packed while far geometry stays shader-driven and cheap. Every shot is checked by rendering 3 test frames at 50% resolution and reviewing them for palette, readability and empty-looking areas before the final render.
concepts.risks:
RENDER TIME: about 720 frames at an estimated 25-40 s/frame at 2560x1440 is roughly 5-7 h. The heaviest shots are S1 and S6 (dense grass close-ups). Mitigations: separate per-shot scenes with only their hero patch; scatter limited to the path corridor; TAA reduced to 32 in fast-moving shots (S2, S5), where motion blur hides it; raytracing at half or quarter resolution; no volumetrics (aerial haze comes from the mist pass instead); Glare done in the compositor. Measure s/frame on 3 frames per shot first. If the average is under 20 s, consider 3840x2160; if it is over 45 s, cut grass density and samples.
LAPTOP SAFETY (explicit user request: do not crash the machine and do not conflict with other Blender jobs): before every test or final render, list running blender.exe processes and their CPU/RAM. Never start a render while another heavy Blender job is using most of the CPU or GPU; wait or use fewer threads instead. Run exactly ONE Blender instance from this pipeline at a time, with no parallel frame workers. Launch with BelowNormal process priority and --threads 6-8 (of 16) to leave headroom. The Radeon 780M uses shared system RAM, so keep the scene's GPU memory modest: 1K/2K Poly Haven textures only (never 4K/8K), instances never realized, about 40 point lights at most per shot, low-resolution light probe bakes. A watchdog pauses rendering if free RAM drops below about 12 GB. Render to PNG sequences with overwrite off and placeholders on, in per-shot chunks, so a crash or driver reset loses at most one frame and the job resumes. Use a unique project folder and filenames, never touch other jobs' .blend files or outputs, never kill other processes. Run test renders at 50% resolution.
GPU DRIVER TIMEOUTS: very heavy single frames on an integrated GPU can trigger a Windows TDR reset. Keep per-frame GPU work bounded (as above) and test the worst frame of each shot before batching.
MÖBIUS AND FRAME MATH ERRORS: risk of seams, normal flips, or train or camera drifting off the rail. Mitigations: one map() function used for everything; a wireframe or ID-colour debug render of the whole loop first; the seam placed in an unvisited night stretch, where a mismatch of 1-2 m is invisible at S4 distance.
CORKSCREW DISORIENTATION OR NAUSEA: limit the roll to 180 degrees in 3 s with eased start and end, and keep the train perfectly stable as the visual anchor.
SCALE READABILITY: the world could read as a toy. Mitigations: haze strength tied to distance, the train and pylons as known scale references, tree sizes 10-25 m, and a 35 to 50 mm zoom for the reveal.
EMISSION NOT LIGHTING THE NIGHT SIDE IN EEVEE: add small soft point lights at the lantern clusters near the camera and a violet world fill; do not rely on emissive GI.
WATER LOOKING CHEAP WITHOUT A FLUID SIM: strong flowing normals plus foam emission plus spray particles plus motion blur, and keep the water in motion and partly framed by the camera move.
SCATTER POPPING OR FLICKER: scatter is computed once per shot from the whole path (not per frame) with stable seeds.
POLY HAVEN ASSETS CLASHING WITH THE PALETTE OR LOOKING LOW-DETAIL IN EXTREME CLOSE-UP: re-tint every material; use procedural GN grass for anything within 3 m of the lens.
OVER-SATURATION OR BANDING: AgX Punchy plus compositor saturation in moderation, 16-bit output, a slight grain before encoding, H.265 at high bitrate.
LOOP MISMATCH: difference frames 720 and 1 numerically and adjust the S6 curve until the difference is negligible.
concepts.audio_plan:
All audio is downloaded from royalty-free or CC sources (Pixabay Music and SFX under the Pixabay Content License, Mixkit Free License, OpenGameArt or Freesound CC0, incompetech CC BY 4.0 with credit). Nothing is synthesized. Keep a credits.txt with the URL, author and licence for each file. Download into a dedicated, empty assets folder.
MUSIC: hybrid cinematic, orchestral strings plus a pulsing electronic arpeggio. Mood arc: curious wonder, then tension (sub-drop and riser), then a euphoric open reveal, then a light pulse that can loop. Around 100-120 BPM, with a strong downbeat to cut on at 4.5 s, a riser peaking at about 15.5 s, and a breath or air section from 20.5 to 22.5 s. Search terms: Pixabay 'cinematic wonder', 'epic ambient electronic', 'space discovery cinematic', 'uplifting hybrid trailer'; Mixkit 'Cinematic' category; fallback incompetech, filtered by 'epic' or 'mysterious' plus a tempo match. Edit with ffmpeg: trim to 30 s, align the hit to 15.5 s (cut 15.5 s before the hit), duck -6 dB under the 6-9 s sunset boom, and crossfade the last 0.5 s into the opening bar so the loop is seamless.
SFX (start times in seconds):
0.0-4.5 light meadow wind plus soft distant insects (Pixabay 'meadow ambience' or 'summer field wind'); this same bed returns at 27-30 for the loop.
1.6-3.0 maglev pass-by: electric hum plus doppler whoosh ('sci-fi train pass by', 'fast whoosh electric'), panned left to right overhead.
4.5 hard cut: wind rush plus continuous rail hum ('high speed train interior hum', 'wind rush').
6.0-9.0 deep reverse-cymbal or riser swell ('cinematic riser', 'reverse whoosh') plus a low rumble ('earth rumble').
8.0 sub drop or boom as the sun disappears ('cinematic boom low').
8.8 three quick electric click/buzz stutters as the windows light ('neon light flicker', 'power on').
10.0-12.8 night ambience: crickets and frogs ('night crickets ambience'), soft river flow ('stream water').
11.5-13.0 waterfall roar building ('waterfall close').
12.8-14.6 big water-rush whoosh during the rim wrap ('water whoosh', 'swoosh down').
14.6 bright impact plus shimmer for the daylight blast ('cinematic hit', 'magic shimmer').
15.5 music hit plus a deep 'cinematic boom' layered.
15.5-22.5 airy space drone ('space ambience', 'deep space drone'); the distant waterfall fades out by 17 s.
22.5 dive whoosh ('fast whoosh').
24.0 and 25.3 rock pass-bys with doppler ('rock whoosh', 'debris fly by').
26.4 heavy swish for the boulder wipe ('swoosh transition').
26.5-30.0 deceleration wind fades into the same meadow bed as 0.0; the maglev hum rises from about 28.5 s so the loop into 0.0 is continuous.
Mix: music at -14 LUFS integrated for the whole piece, SFX sitting under the music except at 8.0, 14.6 and 15.5. Export AAC 320 kbps muxed with the video.

concepts.title: THE DAWN WORKS
concepts.logline: Before every sunrise, a colossal brutalist machine hidden in a black basalt canyon gathers the last starlight, splits it into seven rivers of liquid colour that wake a sleeping bioluminescent wilderness, and pours them over a cliff. The rivers fall up into the sky, where they wind together into the morning sun. The world isn't lit by the dawn. It makes the dawn.
concepts.surprise:
Three escalating surprises, each one changing what the viewer understood before it.
(1) 7.4 s, THE FIRST COLOUR: the first 7 seconds are strictly near-monochrome (saturation about 0.05, blue-grey moonlight only). When the white beam hits the prism, seven fully saturated beams fan out and the screen floods with colour all at once. Audiences feel it physically because they did not realise the film had been grey.
(2) 21.0 s, GRAVITY BREAKS: the seven rivers race to a 1 km cliff edge above a sea of clouds. Everything is set up for a giant waterfall, but the rivers curl backwards over the lip and fall UPWARD, braiding into a helix as they climb into the dark sky. The sound is a reversed whoosh and a sub drop, cut against expectation.
(3) 27.5 s, THE SUN IS MANUFACTURED: in the final wide shot the rising ribbons converge on the horizon, wrap around an invisible sphere like thread on a spool, and ignite into the sun. The sky blooms from indigo to magenta and tangerine in two seconds. This changes the meaning of the whole film after the fact: the machine is a factory that makes dawn.
Grace note, 29.2 s: far below, the machine's tiny red warning lights blink off one by one, and a single collector dish slowly turns away from the stars toward the new sun. The shift is over.
concepts.palette:
BASE (night, shots 1 to 2a): Obsidian Ink #07080F (blacks), Basalt Grey #2A2D36, Moon Slate #5B6378, Starlight White #F4F6FF (the only bright value before 7.4 s), plus Aviation Red #FF2A1A, used only as tiny blinking pin-lights.
THE SEVEN RIVERS (the only saturated colours in the film; each lives in its own channel): Ultraviolet #6A1BFF, Cobalt #1F4BFF, Electric Cyan #19E3FF (kept the smallest and least frequent, so there is never a teal-led look), Acid Lime #B6FF2E, Lemon Flare #FFE81F, Tangerine #FF7A00, Hyper Magenta #FF1F8E. Magenta is the machine's signature colour because it does not exist in the natural spectrum. It is the hero river followed in the FPV chase.
DAWN: Sky Indigo #1A0E4A blending through Orchid #B23CFF and Sunrise Coral #FF5E5B to Molten Tangerine #FF9A1F at the horizon. The sun core is white-hot #FFF6EE, with a magenta-tangerine halo.
LIGHTING MOOD: Act 1 is cold, silent moonlight from a high key (about 8000 K equivalent, blue-grey) with low height fog and almost no contrast. Act 2 (from 7.4 s) is entirely self-lit: all key light comes from emissive rivers, beams and fungi, with real raytraced colour spill onto wet black rock and polished concrete. Hot cores bloom to white and fall off into saturated edges. Act 3 is strong backlight from the newly made sun: long magenta and tangerine rim light, and cloud tops lit from below by the rising ribbons. Grading: AgX with the Punchy look (or Khronos PBR Neutral if tests show AgX desaturating the neon too much), deep but not crushed blacks, no teal-orange grade, no metallic gold anywhere. Metals are black anodised steel, raw zinc and white ceramic.

shots.description: COLLECT. Pre-dawn, near-monochrome. A black basalt plateau holds about 400 white-ceramic and black-steel starlight-collector dishes in staggered hex rows, all slowly rotating in a wave to face the zenith. As each dish locks on, a hair-thin filament of white starlight draws down from the sky into its feed horn. Red aviation lamps blink out of phase across the field. Thin height fog. Silent, immense, slightly eerie. In the last 0.5 s the nearest filament fills frame center.
shots.camera: 35 mm, 1.2 m above ground, slow dolly forward at about 3 m/s between two dish rows with a 2 degree roll drift and a rack focus from a foreground dish strut (f/2.8) to the deep field. Ends on a match-cut: the white filament entering the nearest feed horn becomes the white beam in shot 2.
shots.key_elements: GN-instanced collector asset (screw-modifier parabolic dish, wireframe-modifier truss mast, bevelled hub, cable curves, about 20k tris each), per-instance rotation delay driven by distance, emissive filaments (Trim Curve + Curve to Mesh), blinking red lamps (frame plus ID offset modulo), Poly Haven rock-ground PBR on a displaced terrain, scattered Poly Haven boulders, desaturated moonlit night HDRI plus procedural Voronoi star field, compositor mist-pass fog

shots.description: DISTIL. Inside the mountain: a 60 m ribbed brutalist concrete hall, a cathedral of industry with no religious language. Gantries, grated catwalks, 120 pipe runs with flanges every 2 m, thousands of bolts, stencilled vat numbers 01 to 07. The collected white light runs down a central shaft as a single blinding beam into a 14 m faceted crystal prism hung in a black steel cradle. At 7.4 s it SPLITS: seven saturated beams fan out across the hall and strike seven turbine-vats, which ignite one after another in their colours. Their bladed rotors spin up and throw coloured light across the ribbed vault. FIRST COLOUR OF THE FILM.
shots.camera: 24 mm crane-down from 40 m, descending past catwalk railings in the foreground (parallax), then a 30 degree orbit around the prism as the split happens. The final 0.6 s pushes into the magenta beam until it fills the frame (magenta flash wipe into shot 3).
shots.key_elements: Array-modifier vault ribs, Poly Haven concrete and metal PBR, bezier pipes with bevel depth and GN-instanced flange rings, GN bolts on panel edges, catwalk grating (alpha-mapped procedural grid) with array-modifier railings, one hero raytraced-glass prism with an emissive inner core, fake volumetric beams (emissive cones with fresnel and gradient alpha falloff), 7 turbine-vats (radial array blades, driver-animated spin, emissive slots), coloured area lights placed under the beams for real GI spill, one small low-res volume cube for haze

shots.description: RELEASE. A sluice gate in the canyon wall slams open and the seven rivers of liquid light burst out into carved parallel channels that cascade down terraced black-basalt spillways. As the leading edge of each river passes, the dormant canyon WAKES in a travelling wave: bioluminescent mushroom colonies, crystal clusters, glassy ferns and moss mats light up in that river's colour, rippling outward from the banks. The gradient of colour across the canyon builds up as the rivers diverge.
shots.camera: 16 mm FPV-style chase 0.5 m above the hero MAGENTA river, locked to its leading edge, banking through two S-curves, with a 1 s altitude pop at 13 s revealing all seven rivers fanning across the canyon floor. Then it dives back down. Motion blur shutter 0.5.
shots.key_elements: Canyon walls built from Poly Haven cliff models (coastal_cliff, rock_face, namaqualand_cliff) instanced along a spline at large scale, displaced terrain with rock PBR and a wet-roughness mask, 7 channel curves (U-profile channel mesh plus flat emissive liquid ribbon with scrolling noise flow texture along a stored U attribute), leading-edge mask driven by a single animated 'front' value, GN scatter of about 40k instances (procedural mushrooms, hexagonal crystal clusters, Poly Haven ferns, grass clumps and moss) carrying an 'arrival' attribute so emission ignites as the front passes, point lights riding each front for real GI on the rock

shots.description: BLOOM. Macro detail showcase. A fallen dead trunk on the riverbank covered in procedural shelf fungi and tiny crystal growths. The magenta wavefront arrives and colour climbs up through the translucent gills, layer by layer. Thousands of glowing spores lift off and drift upward in slow spirals, catching the light. Droplets of liquid light bead along fern edges in the background.
shots.camera: 100 mm macro, 20 cm lateral slider move, f/1.4. Rack focus from a single spore at 15 cm to the gill underside of the largest fungus, then a final focus pull to the rising spores. Exit: a spore rises out of the top of frame (motion cut into shot 5).
shots.key_elements: Poly Haven dead trunk or stump hero asset with 4K textures (only shot with 4K maps), bracket fungi built from solidified half-disc stacks with radial array gills and emission plus translucency, GN crystal growths, spores as about 6k GN points with deterministic noise-offset motion (no simulation) instanced as tiny emissive icospheres, Poly Haven moss and fern assets, shallow-DOF bokeh from the river behind

shots.description: THE FALL UPWARD (key surprise). The canyon ends at a sheer 1 km cliff lip above a sea of clouds under an indigo pre-dawn sky. The seven rivers race to the edge in parallel. The audience expects a waterfall. At 21.0 s the rivers curl back over the lip and fall UP, peeling into the sky as seven luminous ribbons that braid into a rising helix. Droplets of light shed upward off their edges, and the cloud tops below light up in shifting colours.
shots.camera: 28 mm, starts low behind the lip looking out over the cloud sea with the rivers passing either side of the lens. As they lift, the camera does an 80 degree tilt-up with a boom-up to follow the braid climbing into the sky, ending almost straight up into the helix. Cut on motion.
shots.key_elements: Cliff-edge set built from the same canyon kit, cloud sea as a large multi-octave displaced mesh with translucent, softly scattering shader (no full volumetric), river curves continuing into a GN parametric helix (position offset rotated around the tangent by t times twist), animated trim so the ribbons climb, GN droplet points shed along the ribbons, world-shader indigo sky with stars fading, coloured lights under the cloud surface following the ribbons

shots.description: DAWN. Extreme wide from far out over the cloud sea: the braided ribbons arc across the whole sky toward the horizon, converge, and wind around an invisible sphere like thread on a spool. At 27.5 s it IGNITES and becomes the sun. The sky blooms from indigo through orchid and coral to tangerine in two seconds, and the cloud sea catches fire with rim light. Small and far away, the canyon machine's red lamps blink off one by one and a single collector dish turns toward the new sun. Hold. A minimal title fades in: THE DAWN WORKS.
shots.camera: 40 mm from about 2 km out, slow push-in with a gentle rise. Locked-off feel for the ignition, with a subtle 1% scale drift after the flash. Final 1 s hold on title.
shots.key_elements: Same cloud sea, the sky world-shader gradient animated over time, GN spiral wrap projecting the ribbon curves onto a sphere surface, sphere emission ramp from 0 to about 60 with Glare streaks and lens dispersion at ignition, distant canyon silhouette with the blinking-off lamp instances and one rotating dish, thin-weight text object for the title (emissive white, fades in)

concepts.build_plan:
ARCHITECTURE: one shared Python module (dawnlib.py) holds the material factory, the GN node-group builders and the Poly Haven fetch/cache helpers. There are three SET scripts, each saving its own small .blend: (A) PLATEAU + SKY, used for shots 1 and 6 as the distant background; (B) HALL, used for shot 2; (C) CANYON + CLIFF + CLOUD SEA, used for shots 3, 4, 5 and 6. Each shot is a camera and timing script on top of its set, so we build 3 environments for 6 shots. Every shot-level animation is driven by ONE custom property per shot ('front', 'split', 'rise', 'ignite') read by GN and shaders. This keeps timing to edit in one place and makes previz re-timing trivial.
POLY HAVEN (via API, 2K textures by default, 1K for distant, 4K only for the shot-4 hero trunk): models coastal_cliff, rock_face, namaqualand_cliff, a few boulders and rocks, dead trunk, fern and grass clumps, moss; textures for rock ground, wet rock, concrete (board-formed and plain), rusty/painted metal, bark; one moonlit or night HDRI (desaturated, used only for reflections and ambient), with procedural sky gradients on top.
HARD SURFACE: collector dish = Bezier parabola profile + Screw modifier + Solidify + Bevel (3 segments, harden normals); mast = low-poly cylinder + Wireframe modifier for truss; hall ribs = one rib profile + Array along a curve; pipes = bezier curves with bevel depth, plus GN Resample Curve every 2 m with instanced flange rings and bolt circles; catwalks = Array of a grating module (procedural grid alpha) with arrayed railing posts; bolts via GN instancing on edge-split panel seams; turbine-vats = cylinders with radial-array blades, emissive slot rings and driver spin; stencil numbers 01 to 07 as text objects converted to mesh, slightly inset. Bevel modifiers on everything visible, so edges catch the coloured highlights.
ORGANIC BY NOISE: terrain = subdivided grid + Displace (multi-octave noise) + rock PBR with a wetness mask from a noise texture; canyon walls = Poly Haven cliffs instanced along a spline with random yaw/scale and overlap to hide seams; mushrooms = GN (cone stem + flattened UV sphere cap + radial gill fins), with randomised cap tilt and size clustered by a noise density field; crystals = 6-vertex cylinders with scaled-in tips, random tilt within a cone, clustered; shelf fungi = stacked solidified half-discs with gill arrays; spores and droplets = GN points with deterministic noise-offset motion driven by the scene time (no simulation caches).
LIGHT AS GEOMETRY: rivers = channel curve -> Curve to Mesh (flat ribbon), with a stored U (length parameter) attribute. The shader is emission = river colour x (scrolling noise flow + wave texture streaks) x smoothstep(front - U), with a white-hot leading lip. Wake ignition: each scattered instance stores 'arrival' = U of the nearest channel point (Geometry Proximity + Sample Nearest), and emission = ramp(clamp((front - arrival) x k)) x river colour x flicker noise. Beams = cones/cylinders with emission x fresnel x gradient alpha (fake volumetrics). Prism split = one hero glass object with the beams modelled as geometry (EEVEE has no dispersion, so the split is art-directed). Upward rivers = GN helix offset of the channel-end curves + animated Trim. Sun = spiral-projected curves on a sphere + emissive sphere ramp.
LIGHTING AND GI: EEVEE raytracing (screen-trace + light-probe sphere/volume fallback) so emissive surfaces bounce colour. A few real point/area lights are animated with each wavefront and beam (hidden from camera) to guarantee strong, clean colour spill on rock and concrete. Bake one irradiance volume per set.
COMPOSITOR: mist pass mix for depth haze (instead of heavy volumetrics), Glare node (Bloom) for neon cores, a few-percent Lens Distortion dispersion (on theme with prisms), soft vignette, AgX Punchy. Per-shot exposure keys.
OUTPUT: 2560x1440, 24 fps, 720 frames, rendered as 16-bit PNG sequences per shot (resumable), assembled and muxed with ffmpeg (H.264 high-bitrate master plus ProRes/PNG archive), audio mixed in ffmpeg.
concepts.detail_strategy:
THREE SCALES OF DETAIL EVERYWHERE: (1) Macro silhouette from scaled Poly Haven cliff kits and big brutalist forms with strong graphic shapes. (2) Meso density from GN instancing: about 400 dishes, about 120 pipe runs with thousands of flanges and bolts, catwalk grating, 7 bladed turbines (48 blades each), about 40k bioluminescent instances in the canyon, about 6k spores in the macro shot. All instances stay instances, never realised, so they are almost free in memory. (3) Micro surface from Poly Haven PBR normal and roughness maps, a wetness and roughness-breakup mask on rock (so the coloured light produces sharp, sparkling reflections), and edge wear via geometry-pointiness and AO masks on metal and concrete.
CLEAN AND PREMIUM: bevels on every hard edge (catch-lights are what make CG read as expensive), no noisy textures in flat areas, controlled roughness, deliberate negative space in the dark Act 1. In Act 2 the only light sources are the hero colours, so frames have a strong graphic composition: deep black, then a clean saturated light line. There is one saturated hue per river and colours are never mixed into mud; channels keep them separate until the sky braid.
COLOUR AS STORYTELLING: strict monochrome until 7.4 s makes the saturation hit hard. Colour then literally moves through the world (beam, then vat, then river, then fungi, then sky, then sun), so the eye always has a moving colour front to follow.
MOTION RICHNESS WITHOUT SIMS: everything moves through deterministic time-driven GN/shader math (dish wave, flow textures, ignition wave, spores, droplets, helix climb), so it is clean, stable frame to frame, and has no cache or sim failures.
MACRO PAYOFF: shot 4 is reserved for showing off surface-level detail with 4K textures, layered translucent gills and bokeh. It proves the world holds up at any scale.
QA LOOP: the AI renders 3 stills per shot at full res and inspects them for flat areas, seams, tiling, blown-out cores and empty corners, and adds scatter or bevel detail where frames read as sparse.
concepts.risks:
RENDER TIME (budget 5 to 8 h for 720 frames, so about 25 to 40 s per frame at 1440p): trivial-scene baseline at 1440p is about 10 s per frame, which leaves headroom for real content but not for heavy volumes or lots of glass. Mitigations: only ONE refractive object in the film (the prism); fake beams and haze with emissive alpha geometry plus the compositor mist pass; real EEVEE volumes are limited to one small low-res box (1:16) in shot 2 and are optional. Render samples 32 to 48 (64 only for the macro shot). Motion blur at 1 step. Benchmark 3 frames per shot before committing; if any shot averages over 40 s, drop samples, then shadow resolution, then fall back to 1920x1080 for that shot only. Do a 1280x720 8-sample previz pass of the whole film first (about 30 min) to lock timing and audio sync before the overnight run.
EEVEE QUALITY TRAPS: emission alone may not light surroundings convincingly, so add hidden animated point/area lights per wavefront and beam. Screen-space ray tracing can lose off-screen bounces, so bake light probes per set. AgX can wash neon toward white: test AgX Punchy vs Khronos PBR Neutral on shot 3 stills and keep cores white-hot with saturated falloff. Glare bloom can shimmer, so use a fixed threshold and enough samples. Thin filaments can alias, so give them a minimum radius and add a soft-edge emissive falloff.
COMPLEXITY: six shots in one night is ambitious. Mitigation: three shared sets, one control property per shot, a shared material and GN library, and a build order of canyon set first (it carries 3.5 shots), then hall, then plateau and sky.
HARDWARE SAFETY (the user explicitly asked not to crash the laptop and said other Blender tasks may be running):
(a) Before any heavy step, check for running blender.exe processes (tasklist). If another Blender job is active, do NOT start a parallel render; queue ours to run after, or run with reduced threads only if free RAM is ample.
(b) Run one Blender process at a time, headless (-b), with an explicit thread cap (e.g. -t 8 of 16) and BelowNormal process priority so the user's other work keeps headroom.
(c) Memory: the 780M shares the 62 GB system RAM, so keep scene memory small. Use instancing (never Realize Instances on the big scatters), 2K textures by default (1K distant, 4K only for the macro shot), decimate distant Poly Haven cliffs, and give each set its own .blend so only one is resident. Set a watchdog that pauses or aborts the job if free RAM drops below about 12 GB or a single frame exceeds 3x the benchmarked time.
(d) Render in frame chunks per shot to PNG with overwrite off, so any crash or interruption resumes from the last finished frame instead of starting over.
(e) Do not change any OS power or system settings. Just note to the user that the laptop should stay plugged in and ventilated overnight.
(f) ffmpeg encoding runs only after rendering finishes, never at the same time.
LICENSING: use only CC0 or clearly royalty-free audio (Pixabay Content License, Mixkit free license, freepd CC0, OpenGameArt CC0). If an incompetech CC-BY track is used, add credit text. Keep a credits.txt with source URLs and licences for every file.
concepts.audio_plan:
MUSIC (downloaded, not synthesized): search Pixabay Music / freepd (CC0) / Mixkit for a cinematic ambient-to-epic build of about 30 to 60 s at 70 to 90 BPM. It needs a near-silent textural intro (soft pads or a felt piano note), an accelerating build with a pulse, and a big orchestral or hybrid swell that can land around 21 s, then a resolving major-key bloom. Search terms: 'cinematic ambient rise', 'ethereal build epic', 'awe inspiring cinematic', 'trailer swell inspirational', 'atmospheric orchestral crescendo'. Edit it in ffmpeg (cut, crossfade, short fades) so the downbeats hit 7.4 s (first colour), 21.0 s (fall upward) and 27.5 s (sun ignition). The music stays sparse and low for 0 to 5 s so the silence sells the monochrome world. Alternative if no single track fits: an ambient pad track for 0 to 10 s crossfaded into an epic swell track. Mix the music bed around -18 LUFS, ducked about 3 dB under the three key hits; master to -14 LUFS integrated, -1 dBTP, 48 kHz stereo, AAC 320k.
SFX (Pixabay SFX, Mixkit, freesound CC0, OpenGameArt CC0), with timing:
0.0 to 5.0: high-altitude night wind bed (low), distant electrical hum. 0.5 to 4.0: staggered servo/motor whirs as dishes rotate (3 or 4 layered, panned L/R). 1.5 to 4.8: faint electrical crackle/zap ticks as each filament connects. 2.0 onward: occasional soft beep tied to the blinking red lamps.
5.0: hard cut to a deep industrial room tone plus a steam hiss burst. 5.5 to 7.3: rising electrical drone or riser as the beam descends. 7.4: KEY HIT, a crystal or glass shimmer, a deep sub impact and a low 'whomp'. 7.6 to 9.5: seven staggered turbine spin-ups (rising whooshes, 7 hits panned across the stereo field). 9.8: magenta flash with a whoosh into the cut.
10.0: heavy metal sluice-gate CLANK/latch plus a rush of water (filtered, slightly pitched up so it reads as 'energy'). 10.5 to 15.5: fast FPV pass-by whooshes on each bank turn (11.2, 12.4, 14.1), plus a cascade of tiny sparkle or chime ticks as fungi ignite. 13.0: wider whoosh on the altitude pop.
15.5 to 20.0: macro intimacy, the music drops back. Soft fizz or bubbling, gentle glassy tinkles as gills light up, airy breath textures for the rising spores, one soft low swell.
20.0: cliff-edge wind gust, a distant roar of the rivers. 20.8: everything sucks out (brief silence or a reverse-cymbal pull). 21.0: KEY HIT, a reversed whoosh plus sub drop as the rivers fall upward. 21.5 to 25.0: rising riser with Shepard-style lift, shimmering airy textures following the climbing ribbons.
25.5: big wide air-pad swell. 26.5 to 27.4: tension riser. 27.5: KEY HIT, a cinematic impact boom plus a bright shimmer or sparkle burst (sun ignition), plus a gentle choir-like pad if available in the music. 29.2: three tiny soft 'click' or relay sounds for the lamps turning off (a quiet in-joke payoff). 29.3 to 30.0: long reverb tail, fade.
All files and licences are logged in credits.txt.

concepts.title: NEEDLE DROP
concepts.logline: One continuous ride on a single song. The film opens at the bottom of a vinyl groove whose walls are carved from the soundtrack's real waveform. From there the camera follows the signal through a tonearm, a copper wire, a night city whose towers are the song's frequency bands, and the throat of a stadium-sized speaker. It bursts out over a desert that the bass sculpts into a new record, just as a chrome needle the size of a mountain comes down to play it. The last sound is the crackle that opened the film, so it loops.
concepts.surprise:
1) 4.2-6.5 s, THE SCALE FLIP: the 'alien canyon' (towering glossy marbled walls) is a record groove. A huge faceted crystal rushes up the canyon at the lens and the camera vaults over it. In one continuous pull-back it becomes a diamond stylus on a magenta and ultramarine marbled record spinning on a vermilion turntable. Viewers also realise the ripples in the canyon walls were the music they are hearing (left wall = left channel, right wall = right channel).
2) 13.5-20.5 s, THE CITY IS THE SONG: every tower in the night metropolis is one FFT frequency band of the soundtrack, so the skyline pumps frame-accurately to what you hear. On a kick drum a bass-band tower erupts out of the street directly in the camera's path, and the camera banks hard around it.
3) 22.5 s, THE DROP: inside the speaker, the stadium-wide ultramarine cone slams forward into the lens on the music's drop. The camera is thrown along its streaming radial ribs, which match-cut into wind ripples of coloured sand.
4) 24.0-27.2 s, THE DESERT BECOMES A RECORD: a shockwave ring of saffron dust races outward. Behind it the dunes self-organise into a perfect cymatic (Chladni/Bessel-mode) mandala of magenta, saffron, chalk and ultramarine bands. Craned up to 700 m and top-down, it reads unmistakably as a vinyl record: concentric grooves, a circular saffron mesa as the label, a crater as the spindle hole.
5) 27.8-30.0 s, THE PAYOFF AND LOOP: a vast shadow slides across the rings and the camera tilts up. A chrome tonearm thousands of metres long, the same design as in shot 2, lowers its diamond out of the ultramarine sky. It touches the outer ring at 29.6 s with a burst of dust, and we hard-cut to black on the exact needle-drop crackle that opened the film. The end becomes the beginning, so the film loops perfectly on replay.
concepts.palette: GROOVE MAGENTA #FF1F8E (vinyl marbling, sand troughs, wire pulses); SAFFRON POP #FFB30F (key lights, record label, sand crests, dust); ULTRAMARINE DRIVE #2236FF (vinyl marbling, speaker cone, sky zenith, pigment spokes in the desert); VERMILION LACQUER #FF3A1C (turntable plinth, speaker cabinet, mesas); NIGHT VIOLET #1B0A3F (shadows, city sky, studio void); APRICOT HAZE #FF9A5A (desert horizon, aerial perspective); CHALK #F6EFE3 (marble veins, sand crests, dust); COPPER FLARE #D8642A (wire strands only); plus neutral mirror CHROME, which only reflects the palette. Strictly no teal, cyan or gold. Lighting mood: high-contrast, glossy, saturated. Hard low raking saffron keys with magenta and ultramarine rims on the macro and product sets; emissive-only light and wet mirror streets in the city; a single low apricot sun (5 degrees elevation) under a deep ultramarine Nishita sky for the finale, with long shadows that carve every ridge. AgX with the 'Punchy' look, light bloom on emissives, mist-pass aerial perspective tinted violet (night) or apricot (day).

shots.description: VINYL CANYON. Fade up from black on a needle-drop thump and crackle. We skim down a V-shaped canyon 60 m wide with glossy marbled walls in magenta, ultramarine, violet and saffron with chalk veins. The walls ripple with the soundtrack's real waveform and are scored with fine lathe striations. Chalk-grey 'boulders' (vinyl dust) sit on the flat lands between parallel grooves, and a giant twisted lint fibre bridges the canyon overhead; the camera ducks under it. At 4.2 s a colossal faceted diamond on a chrome beam slides up the groove toward us. The camera rises and vaults over it, looking down as it passes beneath, until the mirror-chrome cantilever fills the frame (hidden cut).
shots.camera: 18 mm, f/2.2, focus pulled 12 m to 40 m to sell macro scale. Starts 3 m above the groove floor and dollies forward, easing from 12 to 30 m/s, with rolling banks of plus or minus 8 degrees that follow the groove's curvature. At 4.2 s it cranes up to 45 m and pitches down 35 degrees as the stylus passes underneath, ending locked on the top of the chrome cantilever with a whip of reflection.
shots.key_elements: GN groove terrain with waveform-displaced walls; 'Marbled Vinyl' procedural shader with coat; Poly Haven moon-rock models as dust boulders; lint fibre made of 24 twisted curve strands; faceted diamond stylus (raytraced refraction) on a chrome cantilever; raking saffron area light with magenta and ultramarine rims

shots.description: THE MACHINE. The camera keeps pulling up and back off the cantilever. The world expands to reveal the stylus riding a marbled record spinning at 33 1/3 rpm on a vermilion-lacquered turntable floating in an ultramarine-to-violet void. Long strip softboxes slide across the chrome. The strobe-dot ring on the platter rim shimmers, and the saffron label reads 'NEEDLE DROP / SIDE A / 33 1/3' (the only typography in the film, placed in the world). The camera arcs around the gimbal pivot, races along the S-shaped chrome tonearm past the knurled counterweight, drops behind the plinth and plunges into the black bore of a nickel RCA output jack.
shots.camera: Starts on a 28 mm lens tight over the cantilever, then pulls back and up while zooming 28 to 40 mm (a subtle dolly-zoom, so the stylus holds its size as the world rushes outward). It arcs 70 degrees around the pivot, then makes a fast tracking move along the arm tube while widening 40 to 24 mm, with heavy motion blur. It ends by diving straight down the axis of the RCA jack, whose black bore fills the frame for the cut.
shots.key_elements: Hard-surface turntable: bevelled plinth, Screw-modifier platter, arrayed strobe dots, spindle, record with anisotropic concentric sheen, text-object label, chrome S-arm, headshell with screws and four coloured lead wires, knurled counterweight, anti-skate dial, cue lever, pitch slider LED, RCA jacks; gradient cove; studio HDRI used for reflections only; 33 1/3 rpm driver

shots.description: THE WIRE. Inside the cable: a tunnel of seven helically twisted bundles of glinting copper strands spirals around the lens inside a glossy magenta insulation sleeve. On every beat, bands of light race forward along the strands, cycling magenta, saffron, ultramarine. The tunnel tightens toward a blazing saffron point, which blows out to white for two frames (cut).
shots.camera: 16 mm, locked to the tunnel centreline at a constant 30 m/s, ramping to 80 m/s over the last 0.8 s. An eased 180-degree corkscrew roll, a little noise jitter, and strong motion blur on the pulses.
shots.key_elements: GN helical strand bundles (7 x 19 curves, Curve-to-Mesh); anisotropic copper shader; beat-synced emissive pulses from a world-Z Wave texture driven by the beat grid; a moving point light at the pulse front; white-out emissive disc at the end

shots.description: EQ METROPOLIS. The camera bursts out of a circular tunnel mouth into a night city. Glossy chamfered towers banded with LED window strips run in a gradient across the city: magenta (bass) through vermilion and saffron (mids) to ultramarine (highs). Each column of towers is one frequency band and leaps and falls with the music, sending ripples down the avenue. Wet violet-black streets mirror everything, red aviation lights blink, and rooftops are dense with HVAC units, tanks and antennas. On a kick at 16.8 s a bass tower erupts from the street ahead and the camera banks hard around it. The avenue ends at a vermilion speaker cabinet ten blocks wide, and the camera aims straight at its chrome hexagonal grille.
shots.camera: 24 mm, easing to 21 mm on the final approach. Exits the portal 2 m above the street and rises to 25 m on a slalom S-curve at 45 to 70 m/s, banking plus or minus 18 degrees into turns. Hard left bank at 16.8 s around the erupting tower. From 18.5 to 20.5 s it runs straight at the grille and threads one hex hole, whose metal edge wipes the frame for the cut.
shots.key_elements: GN city grid (24 x 64 lots, 5 tower archetypes) with heights sampled from a baked 32-band x 720-frame spectrum EXR; window rows placed in world space so towers grow floors rather than stretch; instanced rooftop clutter; puddle-masked mirror asphalt; arrayed streetlights; a 2000-box far skyline; speaker-cabinet building with a GN hex grille; compositor bloom

shots.description: THE CONE. Through the grille into a dark chamber. An ultramarine ribbed paper cone as wide as a stadium, with a chrome dust cap and a corrugated black-violet surround, slowly inhales away from us as the music's riser builds; dust motes hang in the air. At 22.5 s, on the drop, it slams forward: a shock ripple runs through the surround and the motes blast past the lens. The ribbed face fills the frame and the camera is thrown outward, skimming the streaming ribs at a grazing angle (match-cut).
shots.camera: 20 mm with a 5-degree Dutch tilt, drifting 3 m/s toward the cone's lower-left quadrant. At 22.5 s a 6-frame procedural shake. The camera then dips to 0.5 m above the ribs and is flung outward along them at 40 m/s, so the ribs become parallel lines rushing to a vanishing point.
shots.key_elements: Revolved cone profile with 96 real displaced ribs; half-torus surround with 48 corrugations; chrome dust cap; vermilion basket with bolt rings; spring-damped excursion animation computed from the bass envelope; GN dust-mote points; occlusion match-cut

shots.description: THE RECORD WORLD. Match-cut to the camera skimming wind ripples of coloured sand under a low apricot sun. A shockwave ring of lifted saffron dust overtakes the camera and races outward. Behind it, the dunes re-form into a perfect cymatic mandala: concentric ridges and eight radial spokes in magenta troughs, saffron and chalk crests, and ultramarine pigment lines. Vermilion-strata mesas and quiver-tree silhouettes on the rim give scale. The camera cranes to 700 m, top-down, and the whole desert is a record, with a saffron mesa for the label and a crater for the spindle hole. At 27.8 s a vast tonearm shadow sweeps across the rings. The camera tilts up to reveal a colossal chrome tonearm reaching down from the ultramarine sky, its diamond descending; it touches the outer ring at 29.6 s with a burst of dust. Hard cut to black at 30.0 s on the opening needle-drop crackle.
shots.camera: 24 mm, zooming to 35 mm. 23.5-25.0 s: skims 1.5 m above the ripples at 35 m/s. 25.0-27.2 s: exponential crane up to 700 m, pitching from -8 to -88 degrees, with a slow 20-degree yaw so the rings turn like a spinning record. 27.2-28.2 s: holds top-down as the shadow crosses. 28.2-29.6 s: tilts up to -30 degrees while drifting back so the arm enters frame top-right, f/8 deep focus. Ends on the touchdown.
shots.key_elements: Baked 4096-square dune and cymatic height-map EXRs; GN polar-grid ground with LOD; reveal driven by the expanding shockwave front; pigment-band sand shader plus a Poly Haven sand texture for near micro-normals; near-field GN grain instances; dust ring from alpha-dithered sprites; Poly Haven namaqualand/coastal cliff models recoloured as mesas; quiver trees; Nishita sky; shot-2 tonearm re-used at roughly 12,000x scale; touchdown dust ring

concepts.build_plan:
GLOBAL ARCHITECTURE
- Six independent .blend files, each generated by its own script (shot01_canyon.py ... shot06_desert.py). All import nd_lib.py, which holds: palette shader node-groups; Bevel + Weighted Normal helpers; a camera-rig helper (Bezier path + Follow Path with eased offset F-curves, Track-To empty, keyed roll empty, Noise F-modifier shake with keyed amplitude); render and compositor presets; and a Poly Haven API downloader with a local cache.
- Each set uses whatever scale is numerically comfortable: groove 60 m wide; turntable at 10x real scale; city 1 unit = 1 m; desert in kilometres. Micro and macro are never mixed in one file.
- Hidden cuts: each script writes the camera's world-space velocity, heading and roll over its last 3 frames to handoff.json. The next script seeds its path so on-screen direction, speed and roll carry across the cut. Every cut lands on an occluder or flash frame: the chrome cantilever, the RCA bore, the white-out, the hex-grille edge, the cone face.
- Render: EEVEE (check the engine enum name in Blender 5.2 with a probe script). Raytracing ON (screen-trace with fallback, half resolution, fast GI); virtual shadow maps; volumetrics OFF everywhere (depth comes from the Mist pass); motion blur ON, shutter 0.5, 1 step; 48 TAA samples (64 for shot 2); AgX with the Punchy look; output 16-bit PNG sequences.
- Compositor: Glare (bloom) on emissives; Lens Distortion dispersion of about 0.006; ellipse-mask vignette; aerial perspective as a tinted Mist mix; 0.6% grain against banding.

AUDIO-DRIVEN DATA (analysis of a downloaded track, not synthesis)
- audio_analyze.py runs in Blender's Python (numpy plus the bundled aud module, or ffmpeg to WAV plus the wave module) on the chosen 30 s excerpt. It produces:
  (a) 32 log-spaced FFT bands x 720 frames with 1-frame attack and 6-frame release smoothing, saved as a 32x720 float EXR (spectrum.exr);
  (b) bass/kick envelope, snare onsets and a beat grid in beats.json;
  (c) a downsampled stereo waveform for the groove walls.
- Every audio-reactive animation reads these files. No timings are guessed by hand.

SHOT 1 – VINYL CANYON
- Groove geometry (GN): a 400 m gently arcing Bezier, Curve-to-Mesh with a 90-degree V profile plus flat 'land' plateaus. Seven parallel grooves are made by instancing the curve on points along a radial line, then realized.
- Walls are offset along their normals by the left and right channel waveforms. The waveform is stored as a float attribute on a helper mesh line and read with Sample Index, using the curve parameter as the index. On top go lathe striations (a Wave texture banded along the length), low-amplitude noise, and bevelled land edges.
- 'Marbled Vinyl' shader: domain-warped noise (Noise into Vector Math into Noise) through a 5-stop ramp (magenta / ultramarine / violet / saffron / chalk veins), roughness breakup 0.06-0.15, coat 1.0, subsurface 0.25 tinted magenta for depth.
- Dust: 3 Poly Haven moon-rock models, decimated, tinted chalk-grey with a velvet sheen, scattered by GN Distribute Points on the lands and floor with a noise density mask, scale 0.5-6 m and random rotation.
- Lint fibre: a curve resampled with 24 strand curves twisted around it, Curve-to-Mesh, fabric sheen shader.
- Stylus: an octagonal faceted cone (flat-shaded, 1-segment bevel) with Principled transmission 1.0 and IOR 2.4, using EEVEE raytraced refraction on that one object only. Cantilever: a chrome tube plus shank block with an anisotropic shader.
- Lights: a large low raking saffron area light, magenta and ultramarine rim spots, dark violet world.

SHOT 2 – TURNTABLE
- Plinth: a rounded box with a 3-segment bevel and weighted normals; vermilion lacquer with coat and an orange-peel micro-normal.
- Platter: Screw-modifier lathe profile. Strobe-dot rim: 4 rows of tiny hemispheres instanced on circles.
- Record: the vinyl shader plus radial-tangent anisotropy for the classic concentric groove sheen.
- Label: a saffron disc with Text objects, including circular text bent along a curve with a Curve modifier.
- Tonearm: an S-curve with a tube bevel, chrome. Headshell with 4 screws and 4 lead wires in magenta, saffron, ultramarine and vermilion.
- Also: gimbal pivot; counterweight knurled with GN-instanced diamond bumps; anti-skate dial with arrayed tick marks; cue lever; buttons; pitch slider with emissive LED; nickel RCA jacks with a deep bore.
- Environment: a bent-plane cove with a gradient emission from ultramarine to violet, two long strip area lights, and a Poly Haven studio_small-family HDRI mixed in for reflections only via Light Path 'Is Camera Ray'.
- The record spins at 33 1/3 rpm through a driver.

SHOT 3 – WIRE
- GN: points on circles along a 120 m Z line, rotated by a helical twist (rotation = z x twist), giving 7 bundles x 19 strand curves. Curve-to-Mesh with a 0.12 m circle profile.
- Copper: Principled metallic with anisotropy along the strand tangent.
- Pulses: emission inside the copper shader, a world-Z Wave texture whose offset is keyed from the beat grid, colour stepping through the palette on each beat, intensity from the envelope.
- One point light rides the pulse front. An emissive saffron disc at the far end ramps to a 2-frame white-out for the cut.

SHOT 4 – EQ METROPOLIS
- GN grid of 24 x 64 lots, one point per lot.
- Band index comes from the lot's column. The GN Image Texture node samples spectrum.exr at (band/32, frame/720) using Scene Time. Height = random base of 20-60 m + energy x 180 m, with a per-row time lag so pulses ripple down the avenue.
- Five tower archetypes (stacked chamfered boxes, setbacks, cut corners, cylinders) are instanced with Z scale.
- The window and LED-strip shader uses world-space Z modulo the floor height, so towers add floors instead of stretching. Emission is tinted by the band gradient.
- Roof caps are translated to the computed height and carry instanced clutter: HVAC boxes, tanks, antennas with blinking red emissive tips, and logo-free gradient billboards.
- Streets: violet-black asphalt with noise-masked puddles (roughness 0.03 vs 0.35), lane lines, and streetlights arrayed along curves.
- Far skyline: 2000 cheap emissive-window boxes.
- Start: a circular tunnel mouth matching the wire diameter.
- End: a 600 m wide vermilion cabinet with bolt arrays and a chrome hex grille built as GN hex-ring instances, one per hole, with no booleans.

SHOT 5 – CONE
- Cone: a profile curve revolved with GN, with 96 real ribs from a cos(96 theta) displacement. Ultramarine paper shader with sheen and fibrous bump.
- Surround: a half-torus with 48 corrugations, deformed by GN radial falloff from the excursion value. Also a chrome dust cap and a vermilion basket with bolt rings.
- Excursion: the riser sets a negative 'inhale', then at 22.5 s a damped spring x(t) = A e^(-zeta omega t) sin(omega t), computed in Python and keyed per frame.
- GN dust motes get a velocity kick toward the camera on the hit; camera shake comes from a keyed Noise modifier.

SHOT 6 – DESERT
- Height maps: numpy (in Blender, chunked) bakes two 4096-square float EXRs.
  - Dunes: ridged, domain-warped noise.
  - Cymatic pattern: f = J_m(k r) cos(m theta) for m = 8, with J_m evaluated by the integral form (1/pi) times the integral of cos(m tau - x sin tau) over tau from 0 to pi, at 64 samples. Sand height = exp(-(f/sigma)^2), so sand piles on the nodal lines, plus a J_0 ring term so the concentric grooves dominate.
- Ground: a GN polar grid of 2.4 km radius, densest near the camera path (about 2.5 M faces). It is displaced by mix(dunes, pattern, reveal), where reveal = smoothstep of (rFront - r) and the keyed front speed is about 600 m/s.
- Shader: the same maps drive normal and colour bands, by ring index: saffron and chalk crests, magenta troughs, ultramarine spokes, vermilion between. A Poly Haven sand texture adds micro-normal detail only near the camera.
- Near-field grains: GN Distribute Points limited to 40 m from the camera (camera position via Object Info), 3 ico-grain meshes in random palette colours.
- Shockwave: GN points on a circle of radius rFront with jitter, instancing alpha-dithered soft puff sprites and grains lifted by a sine profile.
- Scale cues: Poly Haven namaqualand_cliff / coastal_cliff models with vermilion strata from geometry-Z banding as rim mesas; about 40 quiver-tree instances; a central saffron mesa (the label) and a crater (the spindle hole).
- Sky: Nishita Sky Texture, sun elevation 5 degrees, raised air and ozone for a deep ultramarine zenith; sun lamp angle 0.6 degrees.
- Giant needle: the shot-2 tonearm asset appended and scaled. Its shadow arrives before the arm enters frame. Touchdown spawns a second dust ring.

ASSEMBLY
- assemble.py drives ffmpeg: concatenate the PNG sequences at 24 fps; build the audio mix with a filter graph (music excerpt plus SFX stems, volume automation, low-pass/band-pass automation); normalise loudness to -14 LUFS.
- Encode an H.265 10-bit high-bitrate file plus a ProRes 422 HQ master. Deliver 2560x1440 native and a 3840x2160 Lanczos-upscaled version, or native 4K if the timing tests allow.
- Iteration loop: 960x540 look-dev stills of the first, middle and last frame of each shot, then a 12-frame-per-shot contact sheet, before any final render.
concepts.detail_strategy:
- THREE DETAIL LAYERS IN EVERY FRAME:
  - Macro: strong silhouettes such as the V-groove, the S-arm, the stepped skyline and the mandala.
  - Meso: strobe dots, knurling, screw heads, lead wires, 96 cone ribs, rooftop clutter, window strips, quiver trees.
  - Micro: lathe striations, orange-peel lacquer, brushed anisotropy, fibre twist, dust, sand grains.
- BEVELS AND NORMALS: Bevel (2-3 segments) plus Weighted Normal on every hard-surface object, so each edge catches a crisp highlight. This is the biggest single cue of 'premium'.
- SURFACE VARIATION: every shader carries roughness breakup, and chrome gets faint procedural micro-scratches, so no surface reads as flat CG plastic.
- INSTANCING: geometry stays un-realized for density at low cost: thousands of dust rocks, roughly 1,500 towers plus clutter, sand grains near the camera.
- COMPOSITION: one subject per frame against a darker or simpler ground; colour blocking keeps each set dominated by 2-3 palette colours, so saturation reads clean rather than noisy.
- MUSIC-LOCKED MOTION: all movement locks to the real music (beat grid, spectrum EXR), which gives the film the precision of a top-tier motion-design studio.
- CAMERA LANGUAGE: eased F-curves throughout, with no linear moves; motion blur on; shallow DOF only in the macro sets; deep focus in the finale for the epic scale.
- FINISHING: 16-bit PNG, light bloom, subtle dispersion and vignette, 0.6% grain to kill banding in the dark gradients, AgX Punchy grade with a +8% saturation trim, and an unsharp pass on the final encode.
- READABLE SCALE: aerial-perspective mist, recognisable cues (rocks, quiver trees, the remembered tonearm design) and slow, heavy motion for the giant objects.
concepts.risks:
LAPTOP SAFETY (the user's explicit request: do not crash the machine; other Blender jobs may be running)
- Before every bake or render, list running blender.exe processes and their RAM. Never run two of our Blender renders at once. If another Blender job is active, wait, or run with fewer threads.
- Launch Blender with BelowNormal process priority and a fixed thread count (for example --threads 8 of 16 logical) so the system and other jobs stay responsive.
- Cap scene memory:
  - target a peak under about 12 GB per shot file;
  - Simplify texture limit of 4K (2K for previews);
  - instances never realized;
  - desert mesh capped at about 3M faces.
- The Radeon 780M shares system RAM, so always keep at least 20 GB free.
- Render in 24-frame chunks, each a separate Blender invocation, with Overwrite OFF and Placeholders ON, so a crash or reboot simply resumes.
- A watchdog between chunks pauses if free RAM drops below 10 GB or the CPU/GPU is thermally throttling, and adds 30-60 s cool-downs.
- Numpy pre-computation (Bessel maps, FFT) runs once, chunked to stay under 2 GB, and is cached to EXR.

RENDER TIME (estimates at 2560x1440, to be verified with 5-frame benchmarks per shot before committing)
| Shot | Frames | Est. s/frame | Est. time |
|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | 144 | ~25 | 1.0 h |
| S2 | 108 | ~20 | 0.6 h |
| S3 | 72 | ~15 | 0.3 h |
| S4 | 168 | ~30 | 1.4 h |
| S5 | 72 | ~18 | 0.4 h |
| S6 | 156 | ~30 | 1.3 h |
| Total | 720 | | about 5 h |
- 4K native would take roughly 2.5x as long, so: render 1440p native plus a Lanczos 4K delivery, and re-render only the hero shots (S1, S6) at 4K if the budget allows.
- Mitigations: raytracing at half resolution, 1 motion-blur step, no volumetrics, refraction on the stylus only.

QUALITY AND TECHNICAL RISKS
- Scale and float precision: avoided by building each set at its own scale and hiding cuts behind occluders, with velocities matched via handoff.json. A cut that feels jarring gets a 2-frame flash or occluder and stronger motion blur.
- Stylus refraction looking wrong in EEVEE: fallback is a dark glossy faceted gem with emissive facet glints.
- Audio-reactive jitter or strobing at 24 fps: attack/release smoothing, energy quantised toward beats, and a clamp on maximum height change per frame.
- Desert moire or aliasing of fine rings from altitude: ring width kept at 6 px or more at 1440p, mipmapped EXR, distance-blurred normals, near-field grains culled beyond 40 m.
- AgX desaturating strong emissives in the city: tune exposure and emission strength per band, check with false-colour test renders, and keep emission below about 8 so hues hold.
- Blender 5.2 API drift (GN node identifiers, engine enum, Image Texture float sampling in GN): probe scripts that build one node of each type and print sockets before the real build.
- The colossal tonearm reading as small: shadow arrives first, apricot haze, slow movement, and mesas and quiver trees in frame.
- Music timing mismatch: choose the excerpt so the drop lands at 22.5 s; if it cannot, slide shot 5's timing by up to plus or minus 0.5 s, since all animation is data-driven.
- Downloads and licensing: cache every asset locally; keep credits.txt with source URL, author and licence; only Pixabay Content License, Mixkit free licence, CC0 or public domain; avoid NC and ND licences.

- Search: Pixabay Music for 'nu disco', 'future funk', 'funky house drop' and 'groovy electronic' (Pixabay Content License, no attribution required). Backups: freepd.com Electronic/Upbeat (public domain), then incompetech (CC-BY, credited).
